/-
  KCore (KCORE-SPEC.md §2). The fixed vocabulary of a definition. Frozen layer; imports only the
  library's added names (BuiltinNames.lean).

  **Symbols and sorts are numbers** (ARCHITECTURE.md §8). A sort is a `Srt` and a symbol a
  `Sym`, both natural numbers: the kernel compares numbers natively and strings character by
  character (findings/R1-scale.md). The numbers below `nRegSorts` and `nRegSyms` are the
  **registry**: every sort and symbol the builtin library's modules declare (Builtins.lean), and
  the generated cells', each with a fixed number and its KORE name (`regSortNames`, `regSymNames`).
  The first 21 sorts and 173 symbols are named here, since Hooks.lean and the generic theorems
  read them; the rest are the library's (BuiltinNames.lean). A definition holds the builtins of the
  modules it imports (`Semantics.lib`, and their parameter symbols), and its own sorts and symbols
  are numbered after the registry (Core.lean). No decision and no part of `Step` reads a name;
  names are read only to print the KORE (`emit`) and to translate to matching logic
  (Statements.lean).

  Besides the registry:
  - **the builtin library a definition imports** (`Lib`): the sorts, subsorts and constructors its
    builtin modules declare. They are part of the semantics, not of the presentation: they decide
    which ground terms are values (`#EOF`, `inj{Int,IOInt}(5)`, an `Id` token) and which sorts lie
    below KItem. `wf` checks it is the union of the imported modules' (Builtins.lean).
  - **token sorts** (`Lib.tokenSorts`): sorts whose domain values are their literal strings,
    distinct literals denoting distinct elements: `Id` and `String`; and **byte sorts**
    (`Lib.byteSorts`, `Bytes`), whose values are the literals of characters below 256, one per
    byte.
  - the interpreted Set symbols and `removeAll` (Hooks.lean gives their meaning).
-/
import KcoreSpec.BuiltinNames

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- A sort: a registry number, or one of the definition's own sorts (Core.lean). -/
abbrev Srt := Nat
/-- A symbol: a registry number, or one of the definition's own symbols (Core.lean). -/

/-- `#unboxKConfigValue` and the projections `project:X` of the registry sorts: builtin functions
with no meaning here (no clause, no hook). They occur only in the cells' initial values, which
`emit` writes and `Step` does not read; a rule that applies them is not well-formed. -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def unboxKConfigValue : Sym := 151
/-- `project:X` of the registry sort X. -/
def projectSym (X : Srt) : Sym := 152 + X

/-- `ite`, K-EQUAL's `ite{S}(C, A, B)`: if C then A else B. The library's text declares it with a
sort parameter S, so it has no number of its own there; the registry numbers it after the
library's symbols, as a hook of signature `Bool, KItem, KItem → KItem`. A definition applies it
at a sort S through an own parameter symbol `ite{S}` of signature `Bool, S, S → S` that this hook
implements (Parse.lean, `iteName`). -/
@[match_pattern, reducible] def kIte : Sym := 315

theorem kIte_eq : kIte = 173 + BuiltinNames.nNewSyms := rfl

/-- The predicate `isX` of a registry sort X below KItem (K and KItem have their own, `isK` and
`isKItem`; MInt has none). -/
def regPred (X : Srt) : Option Sym :=
  match X with
  | 2 => some 53
  | 3 => some 54
  | 4 => some 55
  | 5 => some 56
  | 6 => some 57
  | 7 => some 58
  | 9 => some 59
  | 10 => some 60
  | 11 => some 61
  | 12 => some 62
  | 13 => some 63
  | 14 => some 64
  | 15 => some 65
  | 16 => some 66
  | 17 => some 67
  | 18 => some 68
  | 19 => some 69
  | 20 => some 70
  | X => (BuiltinNames.newPreds.find? (·.1 == X)).map (·.2.1)

/-- The constructors of every definition: K's `kseq` and `dotk`. (`#KConfigValue`, which krust's
text declares and K 7.1.337's does not, is the library's when the text declares it: `libOf`.) -/
def fixedCtors : List CtorSig :=
  [⟨kseq, [Srt.kitem, Srt.k], Srt.k⟩, ⟨dotk, [], Srt.k⟩]


/-! ## The builtin library a definition imports -/

/-- The builtin signature a definition's imports bring: the union of its imported modules'
(Builtins.lean). The K prelude's Bool, Int, KConfigVar, List, MInt, Map and Set come with every
definition (krust always imports their modules). -/
structure Lib where
  /-- the library's sorts below KItem (all but the parametric MInt) -/
  sortsBelowKItem : List Srt := []
  /-- the subsorts the library declares between its own sorts (below KItem aside) -/
  subsorts : List (Srt × Srt) := []
  /-- the sorts whose domain values are tokens: any literal string, distinct literals distinct -/
  tokenSorts : List Srt := []
  /-- the sorts whose domain values are byte strings: literals of characters below 256 -/
  byteSorts : List Srt := []
  /-- the library's constructors besides `kseq` and `dotk`, in the text's order, after
  `#KConfigValue` when the text declares it -/
  ctors : List CtorSig := []
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

namespace Lib

/-- The library's constructors of sort KItem, which kompile places with `#KConfigValue` (they come
from builtin modules named before `K-RUST-CONFIGURATION-VALUES`, `K-IO` for `#systemResult`). -/
def kitemCtors (l : Lib) : List CtorSig := l.ctors.filter (·.result == Srt.kitem)

end Lib

   (intAbs, "INT.abs"),

   (kNe, "KEQUAL.ne"),
   (mapUnit, "MAP.unit"),

   (mapConcat, "MAP.concat"),

/-- The interpreted hook of a `hook{}` attribute, if the registry has one. -/
def regHookOf (h : String) : Option Sym := (regHookNames.find? (·.2 == h)).map (·.1)

/-- The hooked symbols allowed in a left-hand side (map patterns). -/
def patternHooks : List Sym := [mapUnit, mapElem, mapConcat]

/-- The list symbols a pattern may apply (`PatVal.coll`): `.List`, `ListItem`, `_List_`. -/
def listPatternHooks : List Sym := [listUnit, listElem, listConcat]

/-- The library's collection symbols a pattern may apply as `PatVal.coll`: the list's, and the
set's unit `.Set`. A set pattern that concatenates (`SetItem(X) S`) is not one: `_Set_` is
idempotent, so its matches are not the substitutions under which it denotes the set. The unit
alone concatenates nothing and binds nothing: it denotes the empty set, as a constant does. -/
def collPatternHooks : List Sym := setUnit :: listPatternHooks

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/Core.lean:
/-
  KCore. The semantic core of a definition (KCORE-SPEC.md §2). Frozen layer: this is what `Step`
  reads.

  A `Semantics` holds:
  - **Sorts and symbols, as numbers** (`Srt`, `Sym`). The builtin registry has fixed numbers
    (FixedSignature.lean). A definition's own sorts are numbered from `nRegSorts` in the order
    `ownSorts` lists them; its own symbols from `nRegSyms`: first the predicate `isX` of each
    own sort, in the same order (`predOf`), then its constructors, its functions and its
    parameter symbols (`ownSyms`). `wf` checks the numbering (`idsOK`). The names (`sortNames`,
    `symNames`) are read only by `emit` and the matching-logic translation; nothing that decides
    or steps compares them.
  - **Typed literals** (`Lit`): an Int, a Bool, or a token's text.
  - **Subsorts**, a strict partial order over the user's and the library's sorts (DefinitionWf):
    `syntax KResult ::= Int` beside `syntax AExp ::= Int` (KCORE-SPEC.md §3). The builtin library
    the definition imports (`lib`) puts its sorts below KItem and adds its subsorts and
    constructors.
  - **Functions** (`Fn`), with their clauses, each with a priority (`Clause.prio`, smaller
    first: 50 without an attribute, 200 for `[owise]`, n for `[priority(n)]`), and `total` for a
    function declared `[total]` (its KORE symbol carries `functional` and a functional axiom).
    The order of the clauses carries no meaning. The generated `isX` sort predicates are functions
    of the definition too (`sortPreds`): kompile writes their equations into every definition, and
    `strict`'s heating and cooling rules call `isKResult` in their `requires`.
  - **Rules**, each with a priority (`Rule.prio`, smaller first): 50 without an attribute, 200 for
    `[owise]`, n for `[priority(n)]`, K's documented defaults. Step.lean gives them their meaning
    (KCORE-SPEC.md §4).
  - **The configuration sort** `topCellSort`, a registry sort: the sort the rules rewrite. A
    configuration's cells are ordinary constructors of ordinary sorts (`<k>`, of `KCell`, takes a
    `K`), its `XCell < XCellOpt` ordinary subsorts; the cell tree they come from is presentation
    (Definition.lean), read by `emit` and the tie only.
  - **Parameter symbols** (`params`): hooked symbols whose hook has no meaning in Lean, and their
    interpretation (`hooks`), for which every theorem holds.
-/
import KcoreSpec.FixedSignature
import KcoreSpec.NatMap

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- A literal: an Int, a Bool, or the text of a token (`Id`, `String`, `KConfigVar`). -/
inductive Lit where
  | int (i : Int)
  | bool (b : Bool)
  | tok (s : String)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

/-- A term of a clause or a rule: a variable, an application, an injection between sorts, an
alias (`p #as V`), or a domain value. `app` applies a constructor, a
function of the definition, or an interpreted hooked symbol (FixedSignature.lean). -/
inductive Term where
  | var (i : Nat)
  | app (f : Sym) (args : List Term)
  | inj (a b : Srt) (t : Term)
  | as (t : Term) (i : Nat)
  | dv (s : Srt) (lit : Lit)
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A ground value (Value.lean has its order, its sorts and its laws). -/
inductive GroundTerm where
  | ctor (f : Sym) (args : List GroundTerm)
  | inj (a b : Srt) (t : GroundTerm)
  | dv (s : Srt) (lit : Lit)
  /-- a finite map of the collection sort `s`: entries `(key, value)`, keys strictly increasing
  in `GroundTerm.cmp`. The sort tells apart maps of different collection sorts with the same
  entries (the empty `Map` and the empty `AccountCellMap`). -/
  | map (s : Srt) (es : List (GroundTerm × GroundTerm))
  /-- a finite set of the collection sort `s`: elements strictly increasing in `GroundTerm.cmp` -/
  | set (s : Srt) (es : List GroundTerm)
  /-- a finite list of the collection sort `s`: its elements in order -/
  | list (s : Srt) (es : List GroundTerm)
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- The kind of a collection sort. -/
inductive CollKind where
  | map
  | set
  | list
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

/-- A collection sort: a sort whose values are finite maps from `key` to `val`, finite sets of
`key`, or finite lists of `key` (a map has a value sort, a set or a list has none: `val` is `none`
for them). K declares one with a hooked sort
(`hook(MAP.Map)`, `hook(SET.Set)`, `hook(LIST.List)`) and its unit, element and concatenation
symbols; a cell of multiplicity `*` declares one (`AccountCellMap`, from its key cell's sort to
its own sort). -/
structure CollSig where
  sort : Srt
  kind : CollKind
  key : Srt
  val : Option Srt := none
  /-- its unit (`.Map`, `.AccountCellMap`), element (`|->`, `AccountCellMapItem`) and
  concatenation (`_Map_`, `_AccountCellMap_`) symbols, which build and print its values -/
  unit : Sym
  elem : Sym
  concat : Sym
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

/-- A clause `f(p₁, …, pₙ) = rhs requires req`, with its priority (smaller first; 50 by default,
200 for `[owise]`). A clause applies where no clause of a smaller priority does; clauses of one
priority are unordered. -/
structure Clause where
  vars : List Srt
  pats : List Term
  req : Option Term
  rhs : Term
  prio : Nat := 50
  deriving Repr

/-- A function of the definition. `total`: declared `[total]` (kompile writes `functional` and
`total` on the symbol and the axiom `∃y. f(x̄) = y`); `wf` admits that only for a function its
check shows defined everywhere (KCORE-SPEC.md §2.5). Without it the function may be partial: where
no clause applies, it is undefined (`Eval.undef`). The order of `clauses` carries no meaning: the
reader keeps the file's, so that printing is stable. -/
structure Fn where
  label : Sym
  args : List Srt
  result : Srt
  clauses : List Clause
  total : Bool := false
  deriving Repr

/-- A rewrite rule `lhs => rhs requires req` between configurations (ensures is `\top`), with
its priority (smaller first; 50 by default, 200 for `[owise]`). -/
structure Rule where
  vars : List Srt
  lhs : Term
  req : Option Term
  rhs : Term
  prio : Nat
  deriving Repr

/-- The library's collection sorts: `Map` from KItem to KItem, `Set` and `List` of KItem. -/
def builtinColls : List CollSig :=
  [⟨Srt.map, .map, Srt.kitem, some Srt.kitem, mapUnit, mapElem, mapConcat⟩,
   ⟨Srt.set, .set, Srt.kitem, none, setUnit, setElem, setConcat⟩,
   ⟨Srt.list, .list, Srt.kitem, none, listUnit, listElem, listConcat⟩]

/-- A parameter symbol (ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3): a hooked symbol of the definition.
`impl = some g`: its hook is the registry's hook g, whose meaning it has (`Hooks.lean`);
`impl = none`: no registry interprets its hook, so its meaning is a parameter of the semantics
(`Semantics.hooks`), and every theorem stated for all `hooks` holds whatever it is. -/
structure ParamSig where
  sig : CtorSig
  impl : Option Sym := none
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

/-- An interpretation of the parameter symbols: for symbol f and argument values, a value or
undefined (`none`). Evaluation reads it only through `Semantics.paramVal`, which keeps a value
only when it has the symbol's declared result sort: a matching-logic model of a symbol
`f : s₁ … sₙ → s` takes values in the carrier of s, so every model is such an H, and an ill-sorted
answer of an arbitrary H is read as undefined rather than assumed away by a hypothesis. -/
structure HookParams where
  app : Sym → List GroundTerm → Option GroundTerm

/-- No parameter symbol is defined anywhere: the interpretation the parsed data carries. -/
def HookParams.none : HookParams := ⟨fun _ _ => Option.none⟩

instance : Inhabited HookParams := ⟨HookParams.none⟩

/-- The data printed of a `Semantics` (its `Repr`, which the ties compare and the literals are
printed with) does not include the interpretation of its parameters: a literal elaborates with the
default, `HookParams.none`. -/
instance : Repr HookParams := ⟨fun _ _ => "KCore.HookParams.none"⟩

structure Semantics where
  /-- the builtin library: the union of the imported modules' sorts, subsorts and constructors
  (Builtins.lean) -/
  lib : Lib
  /-- the names of the definition's own sorts (numbered from `nRegSorts`), without `Sort` -/
  sortNames : List String
  /-- the names of the definition's own symbols (numbered from `nRegSyms`) -/
  symNames : List String
  /-- the definition's sorts below KItem besides the library's: its own (numbered from
  `nRegSorts`) and the registry's generated configuration sorts it has (`genSorts`) -/
  userSorts : List Srt
  /-- the definition's constructors besides the fixed text's and the library's: its own and the
  registry's generated configuration constructors it has (`genSyms`), each with its argument and
  result sorts -/
  ctors : List CtorSig
  fns : List Fn
  /-- the declared subsorts besides the library's -/
  userSubsorts : List (Srt × Srt)
  /-- the sort of `$PGM` (a user sort, `K` or `KItem`) -/
  pgmSort : Srt
  rules : List Rule
  /-- the parameter symbols: the imported modules' symbols no hook interprets (registry numbers),
  then the definition's own hooked symbols (numbered after its functions) -/
  params : List ParamSig := []
  /-- the definition's own collection sorts (cell collections), besides the library's `Map`,
  `Set` and `List` (`builtinColls`) -/
  colls : List CollSig := []
  /-- the meaning of the parameter symbols that no registry hook interprets. Theorems about
  a definition with parameters are stated for every `hooks` (`withHooks`); no decided condition
  reads this field, so a condition decided on the parsed data holds for every interpretation by
  `rfl` (`*_withHooks` lemmas, Exec.lean and Determinism.lean). -/
  hooks : HookParams := HookParams.none
  deriving Repr

/-- The same definition with its parameter symbols interpreted by H. -/
def Semantics.withHooks (c : Semantics) (H : HookParams) : Semantics := { c with hooks := H }

/-! ## The signature the core induces -/

def insertBy {α β : Type} [LT β] [DecidableRel (α := β) (· < ·)] (key : α → β) (a : α) : List α → List α
  | [] => [a]
  | b :: bs => if key a < key b then a :: b :: bs else b :: insertBy key a bs

def sortBy {α β : Type} [LT β] [DecidableRel (α := β) (· < ·)] (key : α → β) (l : List α) : List α :=
  l.foldr (insertBy key) []

/-- One round of the subsort closure: the pairs found, then each composed with the declared pairs
`base`, less those already found. Successors and membership go through tries of the pairs grouped by
their first sort (`NatMap.group`), so a round costs about the number of pairs found times their
successors, not the product of the two lists. -/
def closureStep (base acc : List (Srt × Srt)) : List (Srt × Srt) :=
  let succ := NatMap.group base
  let seen := NatMap.group acc
  acc ++ acc.flatMap fun (a, b) => (NatMap.succs succ b).filterMap fun d =>
    if (NatMap.succs seen a).contains d then none else some (a, d)

/-- At most k rounds, stopping at the first that adds nothing. -/
def closeRounds (base : List (Srt × Srt)) : Nat → List (Srt × Srt) → List (Srt × Srt)
  | 0, acc => acc
  | k + 1, acc =>
    let acc' := closureStep base acc
    if acc'.length == acc.length then acc else closeRounds base k acc'

/-- The predicate `isX` of a sort below KItem: the registry's (`none` for a registry sort that has
none), or, for the definition's own sort numbered `nRegSorts + i`, its symbol `nRegSyms + i`. -/
def predOf (X : Srt) : Option Sym := if X < nRegSorts then regPred X else some (X - nRegSorts + nRegSyms)

/-- The registry's sorts of the generated configuration: the top cell's, its fragment's, the
counter cell's and its `Opt` sort. A definition's sorts are its own or these (`idsOK`). -/
def genSorts : List Srt := [Srt.top, Srt.topFrag, Srt.counter, Srt.counterOpt]

/-- The registry's constructors of the generated configuration: `<generatedTop>`, its fragment,
`<generatedCounter>` and `noGeneratedCounterCell`. A definition's constructors are its own or
these (`idsOK`). -/
def genSyms : List Sym := [topLabel, topFragLabel, counterLabel, noCounter]

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

def sortsBelowKItem : List Srt := c.lib.sortsBelowKItem ++ c.userSorts

/-- The definition's own sorts in their numbering: those of `userSorts` numbered from
`nRegSorts`. -/
def ownSorts : List Srt := c.userSorts.filter fun s => decide (nRegSorts ≤ s)

/-- The first number of the definition's own symbols after its sort predicates. -/
def symBase : Nat := nRegSyms + c.sortNames.length

/-- The definition's own symbols but the sort predicates, in their numbering (the imported
modules' parameter symbols are the registry's). -/
def ownSyms : List Sym :=
  (c.ctors.map (·.name)).filter (fun f => decide (nRegSyms ≤ f)) ++ c.fns.map (·.label) ++
    (c.params.filter fun k => decide (nRegSyms ≤ k.sig.name)).map (·.sig.name)

/-- The declared subsorts between the user's and the library's sorts (the KORE's `[subsort]`
axioms: kompile writes the declared pairs only, `Int < Value`, `Value < Expr`), closed under
transitivity (`Int < Expr`, which the rules use as `inj{Int,Expr}`): rounds of composition with the
declared pairs, until a round adds nothing; one round per declared pair suffices (`closureStep`,
`closeRounds`; NamesApart.lean proves the result transitive). -/
def declaredClosure : List (Srt × Srt) :=
  let base := c.userSubsorts ++ c.lib.subsorts
  closeRounds base base.length base

def subsorts : List (Srt × Srt) :=
  c.declaredClosure ++ c.sortsBelowKItem.map (·, Srt.kitem)

def le (a b : Srt) : Bool := a == b || c.subsorts.contains (a, b)

/-- The generated sort predicates: `isK(K) = true`; `isKItem(kseq(I, dotk)) = true`, otherwise
`false`; for each sort X below KItem with a predicate (`predOf`), `isX(kseq(inj{X,KItem}(V), dotk))
= true`, otherwise `false`. "Otherwise" is a clause of priority 200 over a variable of sort K.
These are the equations kompile writes for every definition (Emit.lean writes those of
`userSorts`; the fixed text holds the library's), read as functions. -/
def sortPreds : List Fn :=
  let tt := Term.dv Srt.bool (.bool true)
  let ff := Term.dv Srt.bool (.bool false)
  let dk := Term.app dotk []
  let otherwise : Clause := ⟨[Srt.k], [.var 0], none, ff, 200⟩
  [⟨isK, [Srt.k], Srt.bool, [⟨[Srt.k], [.var 0], none, tt, 50⟩], true⟩,
   ⟨isKItem, [Srt.k], Srt.bool, [⟨[Srt.kitem], [.app kseq [.var 0, dk]], none, tt, 50⟩, otherwise], true⟩] ++
  c.sortsBelowKItem.filterMap fun X => (predOf X).map fun p =>
    ⟨p, [Srt.k], Srt.bool, [⟨[X], [.app kseq [.inj X Srt.kitem (.var 0), dk]], none, tt, 50⟩, otherwise], true⟩

/-- The functions evaluation reads: the user's, then the sort predicates. -/
def allFns : List Fn := c.fns ++ c.sortPreds

/-- All constructors: the fixed text's, the library's, then the definition's. -/
def ctorSigs : List CtorSig := fixedCtors ++ c.lib.ctors ++ c.ctors

/-- The collection sorts: the library's `Map`, `Set` and `List` (of `KItem`), then the
definition's own (`colls`). -/
def allColls : List CollSig := builtinColls ++ c.colls

/-- The collection sort `s`, if it is one. -/
def collOf (s : Srt) : Option CollSig := c.allColls.find? (·.sort == s)

/-! ## Names (read by `emit` and the translation only) -/

def sortName (s : Srt) : String :=
  if s < nRegSorts then regSortNames.getD s "" else c.sortNames.getD (s - nRegSorts) ""

def symName (f : Sym) : String :=
  if f < nRegSyms then regSymNames.getD f "" else c.symNames.getD (f - nRegSyms) ""

end Semantics

/-- The signature of f among `heads` (the first of that number), by the trie of their numbers
(NatMap.lean): about log₂ of the number of symbols steps, not one comparison per entry. -/
def lookupSig (heads : List CtorSig) (f : Sym) : Option CtorSig :=
  (NatMap.ofList (heads.map fun k => (k.name, k))).find f

/-- `lookupSig` is the list's first entry of the number. -/
theorem lookupSig_eq (heads : List CtorSig) (f : Sym) : lookupSig heads f = heads.find? (·.name == f) := by
  rw [lookupSig, NatMap.find_ofList, List.find?_map]
  simp only [Function.comp_def]
  cases heads.find? (·.name == f) <;> rfl

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/Value.lean:
/-
  KCore. Ground values of a definition (KCORE-SPEC.md §5). Frozen layer.

  A value is canonical, so equal values are equal terms:
  - `GroundTerm.map s es` and `GroundTerm.set s es`: finite maps and sets of the collection sort
    s, their keys or elements strictly increasing in `GroundTerm.cmp`. `keys(M)` and `X in S`
    read them (IMP's declaration rule: `requires notBool (X in keys(Rho))`).
  - `GroundTerm.list s es`: finite lists of the collection sort s; a list is its elements in
    order, so it is canonical as it is.
  - Domain values, including the library's token sorts (`Id`, `String` under `domains`): every
    literal is canonical, and distinct literals denote distinct elements (a token's value is its
    text).
  This file defines their order (`cmp`) and their sorts (`sortOf`).
-/
import KcoreSpec.Core

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/- `GroundTerm` is declared in Core.lean, before `Semantics`, whose parameter hooks return one. -/

namespace GroundTerm

def isInj : GroundTerm → Bool
  | .inj _ _ _ => true
  | _ => false

/-- The order of numbers, of strings (token literals) and of Ints, as one shape. -/
def ncmp (s t : Nat) : Ordering := if s = t then .eq else if s < t then .lt else .gt
def scmp (s t : String) : Ordering := if s = t then .eq else if s < t then .lt else .gt
def icmp (s t : Int) : Ordering := if s = t then .eq else if s < t then .lt else .gt
def bcmp (s t : Bool) : Ordering := if s = t then .eq else if s = false then .lt else .gt

/-- Literals: Ints before Bools before tokens. -/
def lcmp : Lit → Lit → Ordering
  | .int a, .int b => icmp a b
  | .int _, _ => .lt
  | _, .int _ => .gt
  | .bool a, .bool b => bcmp a b
  | .bool _, _ => .lt
  | _, .bool _ => .gt
  | .tok a, .tok b => scmp a b

def andThen : Ordering → Ordering → Ordering
  | .eq, o => o
  | o, _ => o

mutual
  /-- A total order on ground terms (lexicographic on the tree); it only puts map keys in a
  canonical order. -/
  def cmp : GroundTerm → GroundTerm → Ordering
    | .ctor f as, .ctor g bs => andThen (ncmp f g) (cmpList as bs)
    | .ctor .., _ => .lt
    | _, .ctor .. => .gt
    | .inj a b t, .inj a' b' t' => andThen (ncmp a a') (andThen (ncmp b b') (cmp t t'))
    | .inj .., _ => .lt
    | _, .inj .. => .gt
    | .dv s l, .dv s' l' => andThen (ncmp s s') (lcmp l l')
    | .dv .., _ => .lt
    | _, .dv .. => .gt
    | .map s es, .map s' es' => andThen (ncmp s s') (cmpEntries es es')
    | .map .., _ => .lt
    | _, .map .. => .gt
    | .set s es, .set s' es' => andThen (ncmp s s') (cmpList es es')
    | .set .., _ => .lt
    | _, .set .. => .gt
    | .list s es, .list s' es' => andThen (ncmp s s') (cmpList es es')
    termination_by structural a => a
  def cmpList : List GroundTerm → List GroundTerm → Ordering
    | [], [] => .eq
    | [], _ :: _ => .lt
    | _ :: _, [] => .gt
    | a :: as, b :: bs => andThen (cmp a b) (cmpList as bs)
    termination_by structural as => as
  def cmpEntries : List (GroundTerm × GroundTerm) → List (GroundTerm × GroundTerm) → Ordering
    | [], [] => .eq
    | [], _ :: _ => .lt
    | _ :: _, [] => .gt
    | e :: es, e' :: es' => andThen (cmpPair e e') (cmpEntries es es')
    termination_by structural es => es
  def cmpPair : GroundTerm × GroundTerm → GroundTerm × GroundTerm → Ordering
    | (k, v), (k', v') => andThen (cmp k k') (cmp v v')
    termination_by structural p => p
end

/-- The collection `v` as a value of the collection sort `s`; any other value unchanged. -/
def withSort (s : Srt) : GroundTerm → GroundTerm
  | .map _ es => .map s es
  | .set _ es => .set s es
  | .list _ es => .list s es
  | v => v

end GroundTerm

/-! ## Domain values -/

def digitVal (ch : Char) : Option Nat :=
  if '0' ≤ ch && ch ≤ '9' then some (ch.toNat - '0'.toNat) else none

def digitsVal : List Char → Nat → Option Nat
  | [], acc => some acc
  | ch :: chs, acc => (digitVal ch).bind fun d => digitsVal chs (10 * acc + d)

/-- The value of a canonical Int literal's text: `0`, or an optional `-` then digits not starting
with `0`. Anything else (`"05"`, `"-0"`, `"+1"`, `""`) is not a literal. Read by `parse` only:
the core holds the Int itself (`Lit.int`). -/
def intLit? (lit : String) : Option Int :=
  match lit.toList with
  | ['0'] => some 0
  | '-' :: d :: ds => if d = '0' then none else (digitsVal (d :: ds) 0).map fun n => -(n : Int)
  | d :: ds => if d = '0' then none else (digitsVal (d :: ds) 0).map fun n => (n : Int)
  | [] => none

/-- The canonical literal of an Int (`emit`). -/
def intRepr : Int → String
  | .ofNat n => Nat.repr n
  | .negSucc n => "-" ++ Nat.repr (n + 1)

def boolLit? (lit : String) : Option Bool :=
  if lit = "true" then some true else if lit = "false" then some false else none

def boolRepr (b : Bool) : String := if b then "true" else "false"

/-- The text of a literal, as the KORE writes it. -/
def Lit.text : Lit → String
  | .int i => intRepr i
  | .bool b => boolRepr b
  | .tok s => s

/-- The sorts with domain values, and their literals: an Int of Int, a Bool of Bool, a token of
KConfigVar and of the library's token sorts, a byte string of the library's byte sorts (`Bytes`:
the literal's characters are its bytes, so each is below 256). A literal is a value of its kind,
so every literal is canonical. -/
def dvOK (l : Lib) (s : Srt) : Lit → Bool
  | .int _ => s == Srt.int
  | .bool _ => s == Srt.bool
  | .tok t => s == Srt.kconfigVar || l.tokenSorts.contains s || (l.byteSorts.contains s && t.toList.all (·.toNat < 256))

/-! ## Canonical maps -/

def keysSorted : List (GroundTerm × GroundTerm) → Bool
  | (k, _) :: (k', v') :: es => GroundTerm.cmp k k' == .lt && keysSorted ((k', v') :: es)
  | _ => true

def elemsSorted : List GroundTerm → Bool
  | k :: k' :: es => GroundTerm.cmp k k' == .lt && elemsSorted (k' :: es)
  | _ => true

/-! ## Sorts -/

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

mutual
  /-- The sort of a ground term in `c`, or `none`: a constructor applied to arguments of its
  argument sorts, an injection from a subsort, domain values in canonical form; a collection of
  a collection sort of its kind (`collOf`): a map with sorted keys and entries of its key and
  value sorts (a collection sort without a value sort has no maps), a set with sorted elements of its element sort, a list of elements of its
  element sort. -/
  def sortOf : GroundTerm → Option Srt
    | .ctor f ts => match lookupSig c.ctorSigs f with
      | some k => if sortsOf ts == some k.args then some k.result else none
      | none => none
    | .inj a b t => if c.subsorts.contains (a, b) && !t.isInj && sortOf t == some a then some b
                    else none
    | .dv s lit => if dvOK c.lib s lit then some s else none
    | .map s es => match c.collOf s with
      | some k => match k.val with
        | some vs => if k.kind == .map && keysSorted es && entriesOK k.key vs es then some s
                     else none
        | none => none
      | none => none
    | .set s es => match c.collOf s, sortsOf es with
      | some k, some ss => if k.kind == .set && elemsSorted es && ss.all (· == k.key) then some s
                           else none
      | _, _ => none
    | .list s es => match c.collOf s, sortsOf es with
      | some k, some ss => if k.kind == .list && ss.all (· == k.key) then some s else none
      | _, _ => none
    termination_by structural t => t
  def sortsOf : List GroundTerm → Option (List Srt)
    | [] => some []
    | t :: ts => match sortOf t, sortsOf ts with
      | some s, some ss => some (s :: ss)
      | _, _ => none
    termination_by structural ts => ts
  def entriesOK (ks vs : Srt) : List (GroundTerm × GroundTerm) → Bool
    | [] => true
    | e :: es => entryOK ks vs e && entriesOK ks vs es
    termination_by structural es => es
  def entryOK (ks vs : Srt) : GroundTerm × GroundTerm → Bool
    | (k, v) => sortOf k == some ks && sortOf v == some vs
    termination_by structural e => e
end

end Semantics

def Value (c : Semantics) (s : Srt) : Type := { t : GroundTerm // c.sortOf t = some s }

abbrev Config (c : Semantics) : Type := Value c topCellSort

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/Evaluation.lean:
/-
  KCore. Matching and evaluation (KCORE-SPEC.md). Frozen layer.

  1. **Matching is denotational.** A pattern matches a value v under σ when it denotes v under
     σ: `PatVal c σ p v`. With map patterns (`K |-> V M`, several matches) and the non-linear
     patterns kompile emits (a key bound in the k cell and matched in a map), a matching
     algorithm belongs in the checked layer, proved equal to this relation (MatchSound.lean,
     MatchComplete.lean), as `step_iff` does for evaluation. σ ranges over well-sorted
     substitutions (`WellSorted`), as a matching-logic valuation ranges over the sorts of the
     variables.

  2. **Evaluation states definedness** (`EvalTerm c σ t r`, `r : Option GroundTerm`; `none` is
     "undefined", ⊥ in matching logic). `requires` needs it: a clause applies when its
     patterns match and its `requires` evaluates to `true`; it does not apply when they do not
     match, or its `requires` evaluates to `false` *or is undefined* (the KORE premise is
     `\equals(req, true)`, false when req is ⊥). "Is undefined" must be derivable positively for
     the reading of priorities (a clause decides where no clause of a smaller priority applies)
     to stay an inductive definition, so undefinedness is a result: an interpreted hook may be
     undefined (`/Int` by zero, a lookup off the keys), undefinedness propagates through
     constructors, hooks and calls (strictness), and a function all of whose clauses fail is
     undefined there (`Eval.undef`). A non-terminating evaluation has no derivation at all.

  3. **Clauses of one priority are unordered.** `Eval.clause` reads no order among the clauses:
     any clause that applies, with no clause of a smaller priority applying, gives a result. Two
     clauses of one priority, or two matches of one clause, may both apply; that they then give
     one result is a property of the definition (`Coherent`, `Eval.functional`,
     EvalFunctional.lean), not part of the relation.

  `lookupFn` finds the user's functions and the generated sort predicates (`Semantics.allFns`,
  Core.lean).
-/
import KcoreSpec.Hooks

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

abbrev Subst := List (Nat × GroundTerm)

def injNormal (a b : Srt) : GroundTerm → GroundTerm
  | .inj a' _ w => .inj a' b w
  | v => .inj a b v

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

def isCtor (f : Sym) : Bool := (lookupSig c.ctorSigs f).isSome

/-- σ gives each variable of the list a value of its sort. -/
def WellSorted (vars : List Srt) (σ : Subst) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Nat) (s : Srt), vars[i]? = some s → ∃ v, σ.lookup i = some v ∧ c.sortOf v = some s

/-- A function of the definition: the user's, or a generated sort predicate (`allFns`). -/
def lookupFn (f : Sym) : Option Fn := (NatMap.ofList (c.allFns.map fun fn => (fn.label, fn))).find f

/-- `lookupFn` (by the trie of the functions' numbers) is the first function of that number. -/
theorem lookupFn_eq (f : Sym) : c.lookupFn f = c.allFns.find? (·.label == f) := by
  rw [lookupFn, NatMap.find_ofList, List.find?_map]
  simp only [Function.comp_def]
  cases c.allFns.find? (·.label == f) <;> rfl

end Semantics

/-- `f` is an interpreted hooked symbol. -/
def isHook (f : Sym) : Bool := (hook f []).isSome

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- The parameter symbol f's declaration (by the trie of their numbers). -/
def lookupParam (f : Sym) : Option ParamSig :=
  (NatMap.ofList (c.params.map fun k => (k.sig.name, k))).find f

theorem lookupParam_eq (f : Sym) : c.lookupParam f = c.params.find? (·.sig.name == f) := by
  rw [lookupParam, NatMap.find_ofList, List.find?_map]
  simp only [Function.comp_def]
  cases c.params.find? (·.sig.name == f) <;> rfl

/-- `f` is a parameter symbol of `c`. -/
def isParam (f : Sym) : Bool := (c.lookupParam f).isSome

/-- The value of the parameter symbol f at `vs`: the registry hook's (`impl = some g`; a
collection it builds is one of f's result sort, `_AccountCellMap_` building an `AccountCellMap`)
or the interpretation's (`impl = none`), kept only when it has f's declared result sort. -/
def paramVal (f : Sym) (vs : List GroundTerm) : Option GroundTerm :=
  match c.lookupParam f with
  | none => none
  | some k =>
    (match k.impl with
      | some g => (hook g vs).join.map (GroundTerm.withSort k.sig.result)
      | none => c.hooks.app f vs).filter fun v => c.sortOf v == some k.sig.result

/-- The parameters' signatures, looked up by number, are their declarations'. -/
theorem lookupSig_params (f : Sym) :
    lookupSig (c.params.map (·.sig)) f = (c.lookupParam f).map (·.sig) := by
  rw [lookupSig_eq, lookupParam_eq, List.find?_map]
  rfl

theorem lookupSig_params_of_not {f : Sym} (h : c.isParam f = false) :
    lookupSig (c.params.map (·.sig)) f = none := by
  rw [lookupSig_params]
  unfold isParam at h
  cases hk : c.lookupParam f with
  | none => rfl
  | some k => rw [hk] at h; cases h

/-- A parameter's value has its declared result sort. -/
theorem paramVal_sorted {f : Sym} {vs : List GroundTerm} {v : GroundTerm}
    (h : c.paramVal f vs = some v) : ∃ k, c.lookupParam f = some k ∧ c.sortOf v = some k.sig.result := by
  unfold paramVal at h
  cases hk : c.lookupParam f with
  | none => rw [hk] at h; exact absurd h (by simp)
  | some k =>
    rw [hk] at h
    refine ⟨k, rfl, ?_⟩
    simp only at h
    revert h
    generalize (match k.impl with
      | some g => (hook g vs).join.map (GroundTerm.withSort k.sig.result)
      | none => c.hooks.app f vs) = o
    intro h
    cases o with
    | none => exact absurd h (by simp)
    | some w =>
      simp only [Option.filter] at h
      by_cases hw : (c.sortOf w == some k.sig.result) = true
      · rw [if_pos hw] at h; cases h; exact beq_iff_eq.mp hw
      · rw [if_neg hw] at h; cases h

/-- A collection pattern symbol: the library's list symbols (`.List`, `ListItem`, `_List_`), or a
parameter implemented by a map or list one (a cell map's `.AccountCellMap`, `AccountCellMapItem`,
`_AccountCellMap_`); not one of the map pattern symbols, which `PatVal.hook` reads. -/
def isCollPat (f : Sym) : Bool :=
  !patternHooks.contains f && if isHook f then collPatternHooks.contains f else
    match c.lookupParam f with
    | some k => match k.impl with
      | some g => patternHooks.contains g || listPatternHooks.contains g
      | none => false
    | none => false

theorem isCollPat_of_hook {f : Sym} (h : patternHooks.contains f = true) : c.isCollPat f = false := by
  unfold isCollPat; rw [h]; rfl

/-- The value a collection pattern symbol builds from its arguments' values: the library symbol's
(`hook`), or the parameter's (`paramVal`, of the collection's sort), read in the order `EvalTerm`
reads a symbol, so that the pattern, read as a term, has the same value. -/
def collVal (f : Sym) (vs : List GroundTerm) : Option GroundTerm :=
  if isHook f then (hook f vs).join else c.paramVal f vs

end Semantics

/-- All defined: the values, or `none` if one is undefined. -/
def allSome : List (Option GroundTerm) → Option (List GroundTerm)
  | [] => some []
  | r :: rs => r.bind fun v => (allSome rs).map (v :: ·)

/-! ## Matching: the value a pattern denotes under σ -/

mutual
  /-- `PatVal c σ p v`: the left-hand-side pattern `p` denotes `v` under σ. Constructors build
  constructor terms; the map symbols allowed in patterns (`.Map`, `|->`, `_Map_`) denote their
  values (`hook`), so `K |-> V M` denotes the union of the singleton with M, defined only when
  K is not a key of M: the matches modulo associativity, commutativity and unit are exactly the
  σ under which the pattern denotes the map. A collection pattern symbol (`isCollPat`: a list's,
  or a cell map's) denotes the collection its operation builds from the parts' values (`collVal`),
  so `ListItem(P) L` denotes every list whose first element P denotes and whose rest L denotes. A
  constructor's pattern keeps its constructor meaning (`hc`). -/
  inductive PatVal (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) : Term → GroundTerm → Prop where
    | var {i : Nat} {v : GroundTerm} (h : σ.lookup i = some v) : PatVal c σ (.var i) v
    | dv {s : Srt} {lit : Lit} : PatVal c σ (.dv s lit) (.dv s lit)
    | ctor {f : Sym} {ps : List Term} {vs : List GroundTerm}
        (h : c.isCtor f = true) (hs : PatVals c σ ps vs) : PatVal c σ (.app f ps) (.ctor f vs)
    | hook {f : Sym} {ps : List Term} {vs : List GroundTerm} {v : GroundTerm}
        (hp : patternHooks.contains f = true) (hs : PatVals c σ ps vs)
        (hv : hook f vs = some (some v)) : PatVal c σ (.app f ps) v
    | inj {a b : Srt} {p : Term} {w : GroundTerm} (h : PatVal c σ p w) :
        PatVal c σ (.inj a b p) (injNormal a b w)
    | coll {f : Sym} {ps : List Term} {vs : List GroundTerm} {v : GroundTerm}
        (hc : c.isCtor f = false) (hp : c.isCollPat f = true) (hs : PatVals c σ ps vs)
        (hv : c.collVal f vs = some v) :
        PatVal c σ (.app f ps) v
    | as {p : Term} {i : Nat} {v : GroundTerm} (h : PatVal c σ p v) (hi : σ.lookup i = some v) :
        PatVal c σ (.as p i) v
  inductive PatVals (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) : List Term → List GroundTerm → Prop where
    | nil : PatVals c σ [] []
    | cons {p : Term} {ps : List Term} {v : GroundTerm} {vs : List GroundTerm}
        (h : PatVal c σ p v) (hs : PatVals c σ ps vs) : PatVals c σ (p :: ps) (v :: vs)
end

/-! ## Evaluation -/

mutual
  /-- `Eval c f vs r`: the function `f` of `c` at `vs` has the result `r` (`none`: undefined). -/
  inductive Eval (c : Semantics) : Sym → List GroundTerm → Option GroundTerm → Prop where
    /-- A clause that applies decides, when no clause of a smaller priority applies: its
    patterns denote `vs` under a well-sorted σ, its `requires` evaluates to `true` under σ, and
    every clause of a smaller priority fails. -/
    | clause {f : Sym} {fn : Fn} {vs : List GroundTerm} {cl : Clause}
        {σ : Subst} {r : Option GroundTerm}
        (hfn : c.lookupFn f = some fn)
        (hmem : cl ∈ fn.clauses)
        (hσ : c.WellSorted cl.vars σ)
        (hmatch : PatVals c σ cl.pats vs)
        (hreq : ∀ t, cl.req = some t → EvalTerm c σ t (some (bool true)))
        (hprio : ∀ cl' ∈ fn.clauses, cl'.prio < cl.prio → Fails c vs cl')
        (hrhs : EvalTerm c σ cl.rhs r) : Eval c f vs r
    /-- Where every clause fails, `f` is undefined. -/
    | undef {f : Sym} {fn : Fn} {vs : List GroundTerm}
        (hfn : c.lookupFn f = some fn)
        (hnone : ∀ cl ∈ fn.clauses, Fails c vs cl) : Eval c f vs none
  /-- `Fails c vs cl`: the clause does not apply at `vs`: for every well-sorted σ under which its
  patterns denote `vs`, it has a `requires` that evaluates to something other than `true`
  (`false`, or undefined). With no `requires`, no σ may match. -/
  inductive Fails (c : Semantics) : List GroundTerm → Clause → Prop where
    | intro {vs : List GroundTerm} {cl : Clause}
        (h : ∀ σ, c.WellSorted cl.vars σ → PatVals c σ cl.pats vs → ReqFails c σ cl) :
        Fails c vs cl
  /-- `ReqFails c σ cl`: the clause has a `requires` whose result under σ is not `true`. -/
  inductive ReqFails (c : Semantics) : Subst → Clause → Prop where
    | intro {σ : Subst} {cl : Clause} {t : Term} {r : Option GroundTerm}
        (ht : cl.req = some t) (he : EvalTerm c σ t r) (hr : r ≠ some (bool true)) :
        ReqFails c σ cl
  /-- `EvalTerm c σ t r`: the right-hand side (or `requires`) `t` has the result `r` under σ. -/
  inductive EvalTerm (c : Semantics) : Subst → Term → Option GroundTerm → Prop where
    | var {σ : Subst} {i : Nat} : EvalTerm c σ (.var i) (σ.lookup i)
    | dv {σ : Subst} {s : Srt} {lit : Lit} : EvalTerm c σ (.dv s lit) (some (.dv s lit))
    | inj {σ : Subst} {a b : Srt} {t : Term} {r : Option GroundTerm} (h : EvalTerm c σ t r) :
        EvalTerm c σ (.inj a b t) (r.map (injNormal a b))
    /-- A constructor of `c` builds the constructor term (undefined if an argument is). -/
    | ctor {σ : Subst} {f : Sym} {ts : List Term} {rs : List (Option GroundTerm)}
        (h : c.isCtor f = true) (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts rs) :
        EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) ((allSome rs).map (.ctor f))
    /-- An interpreted hooked symbol has its meaning (Hooks.lean). -/
    | hook {σ : Subst} {f : Sym} {ts : List Term} {rs : List (Option GroundTerm)}
        {r : Option GroundTerm}
        (h : c.isCtor f = false) (hhk : isHook f = true) (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts rs)
        (hh : ∀ vs, allSome rs = some vs → hook f vs = some r)
        (hund : allSome rs = none → r = none) : EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) r
    /-- A parameter symbol has the value `paramVal` gives it, on defined arguments;
    undefined if an argument is. -/
    | param {σ : Subst} {f : Sym} {ts : List Term} {rs : List (Option GroundTerm)}
        {r : Option GroundTerm}
        (h : c.isCtor f = false) (hhk : isHook f = false) (hp : c.isParam f = true)
        (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts rs) (hr : r = (allSome rs).bind (c.paramVal f)) :
        EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) r
    /-- A function of `c` is called on defined arguments. -/
    | call {σ : Subst} {f : Sym} {ts : List Term} {rs : List (Option GroundTerm)}
        {vs : List GroundTerm} {r : Option GroundTerm}
        (h : c.isCtor f = false) (hh : isHook f = false) (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts rs)
        (hvs : allSome rs = some vs) (hf : Eval c f vs r) (hp : c.isParam f = false) :
        EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) r
    /-- A call with an undefined argument is undefined. -/
    | callUndef {σ : Subst} {f : Sym} {ts : List Term} {rs : List (Option GroundTerm)}
        (h : c.isCtor f = false) (hh : isHook f = false) (hts : EvalTerms c σ ts rs)
        (hvs : allSome rs = none) (hp : c.isParam f = false) : EvalTerm c σ (.app f ts) none
  inductive EvalTerms (c : Semantics) : Subst → List Term → List (Option GroundTerm) → Prop where
    | nil {σ : Subst} : EvalTerms c σ [] []
    | cons {σ : Subst} {t : Term} {ts : List Term} {r : Option GroundTerm}
        {rs : List (Option GroundTerm)}
        (h : EvalTerm c σ t r) (hs : EvalTerms c σ ts rs) : EvalTerms c σ (t :: ts) (r :: rs)
end

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/Step.lean:
/-
  KCore. The step relation of a definition (KCORE-SPEC.md §4). Frozen layer.

  A rule r rewrites x to y
  when, under a well-sorted σ, its left-hand side denotes x, its `requires` evaluates to `true`,
  its right-hand side evaluates to y (defined), **and no rule of a smaller priority applies to
  x**: for every rule r' with `r'.prio < r.prio`, every well-sorted σ' under which r''s left-hand
  side denotes x makes r''s `requires` evaluate to something other than `true` (`NotApplies`).
  That is the matching-logic reading of
      lhs ∧ ⌈req = true⌉ ∧ ¬ ⋁_{r' ∈ higher} ∃x̄'. (lhs' ∧ ⌈req' = true⌉)  ⇒  rhs,
  the same negated-competitor premise kompile writes for an `[owise]` equation; Γ_D reads the
  `priority` and `owise` attributes into it (KCORE-SPEC.md §4). Whether r' could also produce a
  defined right-hand side does not matter: a rule that applies blocks the lower priorities.
  `NotApplies` is a positive statement (the `requires` *evaluates* to false or undefined), so Step
  stays a non-recursive inductive with one constructor for every definition.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Evaluation

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- `RuleReqFails c σ r`: the rule has a `requires` whose result under σ is not `true`. -/
inductive RuleReqFails (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) (r : Rule) : Prop where
  | intro {t : Term} {v : Option GroundTerm} (ht : r.req = some t) (he : EvalTerm c σ t v)
      (hv : v ≠ some (bool true)) : RuleReqFails c σ r

/-- `NotApplies c r x`: rule r does not apply to x: under every well-sorted σ under which its
left-hand side denotes x, its `requires` evaluates to something other than `true`. -/
def NotApplies (c : Semantics) (r : Rule) (x : GroundTerm) : Prop :=
  ∀ σ, c.WellSorted r.vars σ → PatVal c σ r.lhs x → RuleReqFails c σ r

inductive Step (c : Semantics) : Config c → Config c → Prop where
  | rule {x y : Config c} (r : Rule) (mem : r ∈ c.rules) (σ : Subst)
      (hσ : c.WellSorted r.vars σ)
      (hmatch : PatVal c σ r.lhs x.val)
      (hreq : ∀ t, r.req = some t → EvalTerm c σ t (some (bool true)))
      (heval : EvalTerm c σ r.rhs (some y.val))
      (hprio : ∀ r' ∈ c.rules, r'.prio < r.prio → NotApplies c r' x.val) : Step c x y

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/Statements.lean:
/-
  KCore. What the statements of the specification (KCORE-SPEC.md §9) are built from: the KORE of a
  ground value and its matching-logic pattern (`GroundTerm.kore`, `den`), the parts of the theory's
  constructor, rule and function axioms that do not read the theory (`distLbItem`, `applies`,
  `fnClosurePattern`), a step function and what it is to list `Step`'s successors (`StepFn`,
  `StepIs`), the decidable conditions the statements assume of a semantics (`Semantics.coreOK`,
  which `wf` implies, `Definition.coreOK_of_wf`), what they assume of its functions (`FnHyp`), and
  the named facts the deciders leave open, from which that follows (`CoreObligations`;
  `Obligations`, a definition's).

  The theory itself, `Γ`, is built from `Semantics` in Faithful.lean, which imports this file;
  soundness and completeness over it are stated in Sound.lean (`Sound`, `Complete`).

  - Symbols and sorts are numbers; the translation writes each under its name
    (`Semantics.symName`, `sortName`), so `den` and everything built on it take the semantics.
  - Ground terms are read as KORE by `GroundTerm.kore`: a map as `_Map_` of its `|->` entries and a
    set as `_Set_` of its `SetItem`s, in key or element order (`.Map`, `.Set` when empty).
  - Cons-Dist is refined for two injections `inj{A,N}`, `inj{B,N}` from incomparable sorts with a
    common lower bound (`distLbItem`, KCORE-AUDIT.md §5): their images meet exactly on the elements
    from a common lower bound.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Tie
import KcoreSpec.ClausesAgree
import KcoreSpec.EvalFunctional
import KcoreSpec.Step
import KcoreSpec.Lazy
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Gamma

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

open ML

/-- The symbols of the collection sort `s` of kind `k` (the library's of that kind when `s` is
not one). -/
def Semantics.collSig (c : Semantics) (k : CollKind) (s : Srt) : CollSig :=
  (c.collOf s).getD (match k with
    | .map => builtinColls[0] | .set => builtinColls[1] | .list => builtinColls[2])

mutual
  def GroundTerm.kore (c : Semantics) : GroundTerm → Kore.Pattern
    | .ctor f ts => .app ⟨⟨c.symName f⟩⟩ [] (GroundTerm.koreList c ts)
    | .inj a b t => KoreAML.injP (c.sortName a) (c.sortName b) (GroundTerm.kore c t)
    | .dv s lit => .dv (KoreAML.srt (c.sortName s)) lit.text
    | .map s es => GroundTerm.koreEntries c (c.collSig .map s) es
    | .set s es => GroundTerm.koreElems c (c.collSig .set s) es
    | .list s es => GroundTerm.koreElems c (c.collSig .list s) es
    termination_by structural t => t
  def GroundTerm.koreList (c : Semantics) : List GroundTerm → List Kore.Pattern
    | [] => []
    | t :: ts => GroundTerm.kore c t :: GroundTerm.koreList c ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
  /-- `k₁ |-> v₁ _Map_ (k₂ |-> v₂ _Map_ …)`, `.Map` when empty (with the collection's symbols). -/
  def GroundTerm.koreEntries (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig) : List (GroundTerm × GroundTerm) → Kore.Pattern
    | [] => KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.unit) []
    | [e] => GroundTerm.koreEntry c k e
    | e :: es => KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.concat) [GroundTerm.koreEntry c k e, GroundTerm.koreEntries c k es]
    termination_by structural es => es
  def GroundTerm.koreEntry (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig) : GroundTerm × GroundTerm → Kore.Pattern
    | (x, v) => KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.elem) [GroundTerm.kore c x, GroundTerm.kore c v]
    termination_by structural e => e
  /-- `SetItem(e₁) _Set_ (SetItem(e₂) _Set_ …)`, `.Set` when empty; a list the same way with
  `ListItem`, `_List_` and `.List`. -/
  def GroundTerm.koreElems (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig) : List GroundTerm → Kore.Pattern
    | [] => KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.unit) []
    | [e] => KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.elem) [GroundTerm.kore c e]
    | e :: es => KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.concat) [KoreAML.ap (c.symName k.elem) [GroundTerm.kore c e], GroundTerm.koreElems c k es]
    termination_by structural es => es
end

/-- ⟦t⟧: the AML pattern of a ground value. -/
def den (c : Semantics) (t : GroundTerm) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.den (t.kore c)

def symP (f : String) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.sym (.symbol f)
def sortP (s : String) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.sym (.sort ("Sort" ++ s))

/-! ## The constructors -/

/-- Cons-Dist′, for two injections into N from incomparable sorts A and B whose common lower
bounds are `lbs` (non-empty): `x ∈ ⟦A⟧ ∧ y ∈ ⟦B⟧ ∧ inj{A,N}(x) = inj{B,N}(y) →
⋁_{C ∈ lbs} ∃z:C. x = inj{C,A}(z) ∧ y = inj{C,B}(z)` (KCORE-AUDIT.md §5). True in the intended
model: an injection's value is determined by its core, which lies in a sort below both. -/
def distLbItem (N A B : String) (lbs : List String) : KoreAML.Item :=
  let x : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let y : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  let z : EVar := ⟨3⟩
  let inj := fun (s t : String) (φ : KoreAML.P) => KoreAML.appList (KoreAML.sym (.symbol "inj")) [sortP s, sortP t, φ]
  { label := s!"cons-dist′ inj Sort{A} Sort{N} / inj Sort{B} Sort{N}", rule := "Cons-Dist′"
    names := ["x1", "y1", "z"]
    pat := KoreAML.guarded [x ∈∈ KoreAML.inhOf (sortP A), y ∈∈ KoreAML.inhOf (sortP B)]
      ((inj A N (.evar x) ≡ inj B N (.evar y)) ⇒
        KoreAML.disjList (lbs.map fun C =>
          KoreAML.sExists z (sortP C) ((.evar x ≡ inj C A (.evar z)) ⋀ (.evar y ≡ inj C B (.evar z))))) }

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- The common lower bounds of two sorts (strictly below both). -/
def lowerBounds (a b : Srt) : List Srt :=
  sortBy id ((c.subsorts.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter fun s => c.subsorts.contains (s, a) && c.subsorts.contains (s, b))

end Semantics

/-! ## Rules with their priorities -/

def anyOfC (S : Kore.KSort) : List Kore.Pattern → Kore.Pattern
  | [] => .bottom S
  | e :: es => .or S [e, anyOfC S es]

/-- `∃x̄'. (lhs' ∧ ⌈req' = true⌉)`: the configurations a rule applies to, its variables bound. -/
def applies (c : Semantics) (r : Rule) (rp : RulePres) : Kore.Pattern :=
  let C := srtOf c topCellSort
  let vs := KoreAML.varList (r.vars.map c.sortName) rp.names
  KoreAML.existsAll C (vs.map KoreAML.Var.kore)
    (.and C [Term.kore c vs r.lhs, reqPat C (r.req.map (Term.kore c vs))])

/-! ## The closure axiom of a function (KCORE-SPEC.md §2.5, decision D1 of PLAN.md)

A function's equations say, per clause, `premise ∧ ¬ ⋁ lower → f(X̄) = rhs`, the clauses of a
smaller priority negated (Faithful.lean). Where no premise holds, they leave `f(X̄)` unconstrained:
in some model it is ⊥, in another any element. Evaluation reads such a point as undefined
(`Eval.undef`), and so must every model, or a `requires` that calls f there could be true in one
model and its rule fire there, a step `Step` does not have. The closure axiom bounds f from above,
as the step's closure axiom (`Γstep`) bounds `•`: every element of `f(X̄)` is the right-hand side
of a clause whose premise holds,

    ∀X̄ ∀y. y ∈ f(X̄) → ⋁_i ∃ȳ_i. (premise_i ∧ y ∈ rhs_i)

with each premise the clause's own (`premise`, Emit.lean), the clauses of a smaller priority not
negated: the clause that gives f's value has its premise holding, so the axiom is true without
them. With the equations, it makes `f(X̄)` the value of a clause that applies, no clause of a
smaller priority applying, ⊥ where none does: the least-defined model, the reading KCORE-SPEC.md
takes for the partial hooks. -/

/-- The element `y` of a function's closure axiom. -/
def fnClosureY (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) : Kore.Pattern := KoreAML.ev "Y'Hash'Fn" (srtOf c f.result)

/-- A clause's disjunct: `∃ȳ. premise ∧ y ∈ rhs`. -/
def fnClauseDisjunct (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (cl : Clause) (cp : ClausePres) : Kore.Pattern :=
  let vs := KoreAML.varList (cl.vars.map c.sortName) cp.names
  KoreAML.existsAll KoreAML.R (vs.map KoreAML.Var.kore)
    (.and KoreAML.R [premise (f.args.map c.sortName) (cl.req.map (Term.kore c vs)) (Term.koreList c vs cl.pats),
      Kore.Pattern.in (srtOf c f.result) KoreAML.R (fnClosureY c f) (Term.kore c vs cl.rhs)])

/-- The closure axiom of f, as a KORE pattern over the sort variable `R` (free X̄ and y):
`y ∈ f(X̄) → ⋁ disjuncts`. -/
def fnClosurePattern (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (fp : FnPres) : Kore.Pattern :=
  let call := KoreAML.ap (c.symName f.label) (KoreAML.vars (KoreAML.numbered "X" 0 (f.args.map c.sortName)))
  let ds := (withPres f.clauses fp.clauses).map fun (cl, cp) => fnClauseDisjunct c f cl cp
  Kore.Pattern.implies KoreAML.R (Kore.Pattern.in (srtOf c f.result) KoreAML.R (fnClosureY c f) call)
    (KoreAML.anyOf ds)

/-- A step function on ground values. -/
abbrev StepFn := GroundTerm → List GroundTerm

/-! ## What the statements assume of a semantics -/

/-- **The decidable conditions soundness and completeness assume of a semantics**: its subsorts,
clauses and rules are well sorted (`sortedOK`), the decidable conditions of its theory that the
proofs read hold (`faithCoreOK`), no user symbol is named like an interpreted hook (`hooksApart`),
the functions evaluation reads are named apart (`predsApart`), and its own sorts and symbols are
numbered in order (`idsOK`). -/
def Semantics.coreOK (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.sortedOK && c.faithCoreOK && c.hooksApart && c.predsApart && c.idsOK

theorem Semantics.coreOK_parts {c : Semantics} (h : c.coreOK = true) :
    c.sortedOK = true ∧ c.faithCoreOK = true ∧ c.hooksApart = true ∧ c.predsApart = true ∧ c.idsOK = true := by
  simp only [Semantics.coreOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  exact ⟨h.1.1.1.1, h.1.1.1.2, h.1.1.2, h.1.2, h.2⟩

/-- `okAll`, `faithOK` and the three name conditions give `coreOK`. -/
theorem Semantics.coreOK_of_okAll {c : Semantics} (hok : c.okAll = true) (hfa : c.faithOK = true)
    (hha : c.hooksApart = true) (hpa : c.predsApart = true) (hids : c.idsOK = true) : c.coreOK = true := by
  simp only [Semantics.coreOK, Semantics.sortedOK_of_okAll hok, Semantics.faithCoreOK_of_faithOK hfa, hha,
    hpa, hids, Bool.and_self]

/-- A well-formed definition's semantics meets `coreOK`: `wf` checks each of its conditions. -/
theorem Definition.coreOK_of_wf {d : Definition} (h : wf d = true) : d.sem.coreOK = true := by
  simp only [wf, Definition.namesOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨-, hha⟩, hpa⟩, hids⟩, hok⟩, -⟩, -⟩, -⟩, hfa⟩ := h
  exact Semantics.coreOK_of_okAll hok hfa hha hpa hids

/-- **What the statements assume of the functions of a semantics**: each function has a result at
every argument list of its sorts, each `[total]` one a value there, any two equations of one
priority of a function are coherent where both apply (`ClausesAgree`), and any two matches of a
clause at one argument list give one result (`MatchIndependent`). -/
def FnHyp (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, ∀ vs, c.sortsOf vs = some fn.args → ∃ r, Eval c fn.label vs r) ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, fn.total = true → ∀ vs, c.sortsOf vs = some fn.args → ∃ v, Eval c fn.label vs (some v)) ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, ClausesAgree c fn) ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, ∀ cl ∈ fn.clauses, MatchIndependent c cl)

/-- **The facts `coreOK` does not decide**, for a semantics `c` and a termination certificate `t`:
the functions whose termination neither declaration order nor a decreasing self call at `t`'s
argument shows (`orderObligations`, `Certificates.obligations`) have a result at every argument
list of their sorts, the `[total]` functions `totalOK` does not confirm have a value there
(`totalObligations`), each two equations of one priority of a function `fnExclusiveOK` does not
confirm are coherent (`agreeObligations`, `ClausesAgree`), each clause `clauseFixed` does not show
to fix its variables gives one result at one argument list (`matchObligations`, each a function and
the index of its clause, `MatchIndependent`), and each argument a short-circuiting evaluation may
skip whose value `definedArg` does not show has one wherever it is skipped (`lazyObligations`,
`LazyOcc.Holds`). Each conjunct is over a list of named functions, clauses or occurrences, all
empty in a semantics the deciders confirm (`CoreObligations.of_nil`). -/
def CoreObligations (c : Semantics) (t : Certificates) : Prop :=
  (∀ f ∈ c.orderObligations ++ t.obligations c, ∀ fn, c.lookupFn f = some fn →
    ∀ vs, c.sortsOf vs = some fn.args → ∃ r, Eval c f vs r) ∧
  (∀ f ∈ c.totalObligations, ∀ fn, c.lookupFn f = some fn →
    ∀ vs, c.sortsOf vs = some fn.args → ∃ v, Eval c f vs (some v)) ∧
  (∀ f ∈ c.agreeObligations, ∀ fn, c.lookupFn f = some fn → ClausesAgree c fn) ∧
  (∀ p ∈ c.matchObligations, ∀ fn, c.lookupFn p.1 = some fn →
    ∀ cl, fn.clauses[p.2]? = some cl → MatchIndependent c cl) ∧
  (∀ o ∈ c.lazyObligations, o.Holds c)

theorem CoreObligations.of_nil {c : Semantics} {t : Certificates}
    (h1 : c.orderObligations ++ t.obligations c = [])
    (h2 : c.totalObligations = []) (h3 : c.agreeObligations = [])
    (h4 : c.matchObligations = []) (h5 : c.lazyObligations = []) : CoreObligations c t :=
  ⟨fun f hf => by rw [h1] at hf; exact absurd hf (List.not_mem_nil),
   fun f hf => by rw [h2] at hf; exact absurd hf (List.not_mem_nil),
   fun f hf => by rw [h3] at hf; exact absurd hf (List.not_mem_nil),
   fun p hp => by rw [h4] at hp; exact absurd hp (List.not_mem_nil),
   fun o ho => by rw [h5] at ho; exact absurd ho (List.not_mem_nil)⟩

/-- The named obligations of a definition: `CoreObligations` of its semantics, with its
certificate as the termination certificate. `Obligations.of_nil`: they hold when none is named
(a generated package then states `obligations_nil`; where some are named, its `sound` and
`complete` take them as a premise). -/
def Obligations (d : Definition) : Prop := CoreObligations d.sem d.cert

theorem Obligations.of_nil {d : Definition} (h1 : d.sem.orderObligations ++ d.cert.obligations d.sem = [])
    (h2 : d.sem.totalObligations = []) (h3 : d.sem.agreeObligations = [])
    (h4 : d.sem.matchObligations = []) (h5 : d.sem.lazyObligations = []) : Obligations d :=
  CoreObligations.of_nil h1 h2 h3 h4 h5

/-- The step relation's successors, as a step function (any enumeration of `Step`'s successors;
the checked layer gives the executable one, `Exec.successorsN`, with `Exec.step_iff`). -/
def StepIs (c : Semantics) (ref : StepFn) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Config c) (y : GroundTerm), y ∈ ref x.val ↔ ∃ hy : c.sortOf y = some topCellSort, Step c x ⟨y, hy⟩

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/Tie.lean:
/-
  KCore. The tie between a KORE text and its core (KCORE-SPEC.md §1). Reviewed layer. A KORE
  text k is tied (`Tied k`) when `parse k = .ok d`, `wf d`, and `Reordered d.emit k`: the core
  `d` prints back to k up to the order of its sentences, so what `Step` reads is what the KORE
  says.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Parse
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Reorder
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Translate
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Blocks
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Distinct
import KcoreSpec.FaithOK

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- No user constructor or function is named like an interpreted hooked symbol (`hookSigs`).
Evaluation reads such a name as the hook (`isHook`, Evaluation.lean; the names it reads are exactly
`hookSigs`', `isHook_iff` in HooksApart.lean), whatever the definition declares; when the
definition's imports do not declare that hook, the name would be the user's symbol
in the KORE, with the user's clauses, and the hook in `Step`. Rejecting the name keeps the two
the same (KCORE-SPEC.md §7). -/
def Semantics.hooksApart (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.ctors.all (fun k => !hookSigs.any (·.name == k.name)) &&
    c.fns.all (fun f => !hookSigs.any (·.name == f.label))

/-- The functions evaluation reads (`Semantics.allFns`: the user's, then the generated sort
predicates) have distinct labels. `lookupFn` takes the first function of a label, so a user
function named like a sort predicate (`LblisInt`), or a user sort named like a library sort (two
predicates `LblisInt`), would make "the function f" ambiguous between the core and the KORE. The
declaration check of `namesOK` excludes both whenever the fixed text declares the library's sorts
and their predicates, as the six texts do; `predsApart` states it on the core, where evaluation
reads it (KCORE-SPEC.md §7). -/
def Semantics.predsApart (c : Semantics) : Bool := nodup (c.allFns.map (·.label))

/-- Every sort and symbol the emitted KORE declares is declared once, no user symbol is named
like an interpreted hook (`hooksApart`), and the functions evaluation reads are named apart
(`predsApart`). -/
def Definition.namesOK (d : Definition) : Bool :=
  let D := d.emit
  KoreAML.nodup (D.sortDecls.map (·.name)) && KoreAML.nodup (D.symbolDecls.map (·.name) ++ D.aliasNames) &&
    d.sem.hooksApart && d.sem.predsApart && d.sem.idsOK

def Semantics.ok (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.declsOK && c.subsortsOK && c.inhabited && c.fnsOK && c.rules.all c.ruleOK

/-- The definition is well-formed: as `ok`, with the rules' left-hand sides well-sorted over the
collection pattern symbols too (`ruleOKAll`: a list's `ListItem(P) L`, a cell map's). `ok` is the
narrower condition the executable matcher's theorems read; `okAll` is what the tie checks. -/
def Semantics.okAll (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.declsOK && c.subsortsOK && c.inhabited && c.fnsOKAll && c.rules.all c.ruleOKAll

theorem Semantics.okAll_of_ok {c : Semantics} (h : c.ok = true) : c.okAll = true := by
  simp only [Semantics.ok, Semantics.okAll, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨h.1.1, c.fnsOKAll_of h.1.2⟩, fun r hr => c.ruleOKAll_of (h.2 r hr)⟩

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- A clause of `f` is well sorted over the function signatures `rhsHeads`: its patterns have the
argument sorts in a left-hand side's context (`patCtxAll`) and bind each of its variables, its
`requires` is a Bool and its right-hand side has the result sort. -/
def clauseSorted (f : Fn) (rhsHeads : List CtorSig) (cl : Clause) : Bool :=
  sortsOfTerms c.patCtxAll cl.vars cl.pats == some f.args &&
  binds cl.vars.length (varOccsList cl.pats) &&
  reqOK (c.rhsCtx rhsHeads) cl.vars cl.req &&
  sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx rhsHeads) cl.vars cl.rhs == some f.result

/-- A rule is well sorted: its left-hand side has the configuration sort in a left-hand side's
context (`patCtxAll`) and binds each of its variables, its `requires` is a Bool and its right-hand
side has the configuration sort, over the constructors, hooks, parameters and functions. -/
def ruleSorted (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  sortOfTerm c.patCtxAll r.vars r.lhs == some topCellSort &&
  binds r.vars.length (varOccs r.lhs) &&
  reqOK (c.rhsCtx (c.fns.map Fn.sig)) r.vars r.req &&
  sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx (c.fns.map Fn.sig)) r.vars r.rhs == some topCellSort

/-- **The semantics is well sorted**: its subsorts are a strict partial order into its own sorts
and the library's sorts of constructor terms (`subsortsOK`), and every clause of every function and every rule is well sorted, binding each of
its variables (`clauseSorted`, `ruleSorted`). -/
def sortedOK : Bool :=
  c.subsortsOK && c.fns.all (fun f => f.clauses.all (c.clauseSorted f (c.fns.map Fn.sig))) &&
    c.rules.all c.ruleSorted

theorem clauseSorted_of_all {f : Fn} {H : List CtorSig} {cl : Clause} (h : c.clauseOKAll f H cl = true) :
    c.clauseSorted f H cl = true := by
  simp only [clauseOKAll, clauseSorted, Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨⟨h.1.1.1.1, h.1.1.2⟩, h.1.2⟩, h.2⟩

theorem ruleSorted_of_all {r : Rule} (h : c.ruleOKAll r = true) : c.ruleSorted r = true := by
  simp only [ruleOKAll, ruleSorted, Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨⟨h.1.1.1.1, h.1.1.2⟩, h.1.2⟩, h.2⟩

end Semantics

/-- `okAll` checks each condition of `sortedOK`. -/
theorem Semantics.sortedOK_of_okAll {c : Semantics} (h : c.okAll = true) : c.sortedOK = true := by
  simp only [Semantics.okAll, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨-, hs⟩, -⟩, hf⟩, hr⟩ := h
  simp only [Semantics.fnsOKAll, List.all_eq_true] at hf
  simp only [Semantics.sortedOK, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true]
  refine ⟨⟨hs, fun f hf' cl hcl => ?_⟩, fun r hr' => c.ruleSorted_of_all (List.all_eq_true.mp hr r hr')⟩
  have := hf f hf'
  simp only [Semantics.fnOKAll, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true] at this
  exact c.clauseSorted_of_all (this.1 cl hcl)

def Definition.report (d : Definition) : List (String × Bool) :=
  [("names declared once, none named like a hook, functions named apart, own sorts and symbols numbered in order", d.namesOK),
   ("declarations over declared sorts", d.sem.declsOK),
   ("subsorts: a strict partial order into user sorts and library constructor sorts, closed", d.sem.subsortsOK),
   ("sorts inhabited", d.sem.inhabited),
   ("functions: well-sorted, covering", d.sem.fnsOK),
   ("rules: well-sorted over the configuration sort", d.sem.rules.all d.sem.ruleOKAll),
   ("certificate: self calls decrease", d.cert.ok d.sem),
   ("presentation: variable names distinct; cells named apart, one k cell of content K, each with its kind's sorts and symbols, the core's first sorts, constructors and subsorts", d.pres.ok d.sem),
   ("theory: no function or constructor named like ite at a sort, functions' sorts numbered", Faithful.namesNumbered d.sem),
   ("theory: values generated (constructor sorts)", Faithful.genWf d.sem),
   ("theory: no collection sort holds a domain value", Faithful.collSortsOK d.sem),
   ("theory: collections built by the parameters their names denote", Faithful.collsOK d.sem),
   ("theory: every left-hand-side head a constructor or read downwards", Faithful.patHeadsOK d.sem),
   ("theory: symbols and sorts named apart", Faithful.Model.namesApartK d.sem),
   ("theory: no token or byte sort is Int or Bool", Faithful.Model.LitsApart d.sem),
   ("theory: sorts of values and symbols numbered", Faithful.Model.sortsNumbered d.sem),
   ("theory: collection symbols apart from constructors", Faithful.Model.collsNotCtors d.sem),
   ("theory: symbols named like ite apart by their sort", Faithful.Model.itesApart d.sem),
   ("theory: hooks, parameters and constructors apart", Faithful.Model.kindsApart d.sem),
   ("theory: each constructor listed once", Faithful.Model.ctorsOnce d.sem),
   ("theory: functions apart from constructors, hooks and parameters", Faithful.Model.fnsApart d.sem)]

/-- A parameter symbol's argument or result sort: a declared sort below KItem, K or KItem. Unlike a
constructor's, it may be a sort of which KCore represents no value (List): the symbol is then
never applied, or never defined (`paramVal` keeps only values of its sort). -/
def Semantics.paramSortOK (c : Semantics) (s : Srt) : Bool :=
  [Srt.k, Srt.kitem].contains s || c.userSorts.contains s || c.lib.sortsBelowKItem.contains s

/-- The arguments of a collection sort's element symbol: a map's key and value sorts, a set's or a
list's element sort; `none` when its value sort is not as its kind has it (a map has one, a set or
a list none). -/
def CollSig.elemArgs (k : CollSig) : Option (List Srt) :=
  match k.kind, k.val with
  | .map, some v => some [k.key, v]
  | .set, none | .list, none => some [k.key]
  | _, _ => none

/-- A collection sort of the definition: one of its sorts, with a value sort exactly when it is a
map (`CollSig.elemArgs`), whose unit, element and concatenation are parameter symbols of its sort
implemented by the hooks of its kind (`MAP.unit`, `MAP.element`, `MAP.concat` for a map), so its
values are built and read as the library's collections are. -/
def Semantics.collOK (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig) : Bool :=
  let b := builtinColl k.kind
  match k.elemArgs with
  | none => false
  | some elemArgs =>
    c.userSorts.contains k.sort &&
    c.params.contains ⟨⟨k.unit, [], k.sort⟩, some b.unit⟩ &&
    c.params.contains ⟨⟨k.elem, elemArgs, k.sort⟩, some b.elem⟩ &&
    c.params.contains ⟨⟨k.concat, [k.sort, k.sort], k.sort⟩, some b.concat⟩

/-- The parameter symbols: first those of the imported modules (registry numbers, each one of
`libParams`, Builtins.lean), then the user's (own numbers), whose sorts are declared ones, each with a presentation, and whose meaning
is the one its `hook{}` attribute names: the registry's hook when the registry interprets that
attribute (`regHookOf`), a parameter otherwise; and the collection sorts (`collOK`). -/
def Definition.paramsOK (d : Definition) : Bool :=
  let lib := d.sem.params.takeWhile fun k => decide (k.sig.name < nRegSyms)
  let own := d.sem.params.drop lib.length
  lib.all (libParams d.pres.imports).contains &&
  own.all (fun k => decide (nRegSyms ≤ k.sig.name)) &&
  own.length == d.pres.params.length &&
  (withPres own d.pres.params).all (fun (k, pp) =>
    k.sig.args.all d.sem.paramSortOK && d.sem.paramSortOK k.sig.result && k.impl == regHookOf pp.hook) &&
  -- the collection sorts: distinct, and each built by its symbols
  nodup (d.sem.colls.map (·.sort)) && d.sem.colls.all d.sem.collOK

/-- **A well-formed definition**: its names (`namesOK`), its core (`okAll`), its certificate, its
presentation and its parameters are well formed, and its semantics meets the decidable conditions
of its matching-logic theory (`faithOK`). -/
def wf (d : Definition) : Bool :=
  d.namesOK && d.sem.okAll && d.cert.ok d.sem && d.pres.ok d.sem && d.paramsOK && d.sem.faithOK

theorem faithOK_of_wf {d : Definition} (h : wf d = true) : d.sem.faithOK = true := by
  unfold wf at h
  simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  exact h.2

/-- `Tied k`: k is the emitted KORE of a well-formed definition, up to sentence order.
Irreducible: unfolding it runs `parse` on k, which the elaborator would otherwise do whenever it
compares a type with `Tied k`; the kernel unfolds it all the same. -/
@[irreducible] def Tied (k : Kore.Definition) : Prop :=
  match Parse.parse k with
  | .ok d => wf d = true ∧ KoreAML.Reordered d.emit k
  | .error _ => False

instance (k : Kore.Definition) : Decidable (Tied k) := by
  unfold Tied
  cases Parse.parse k with
  | error => exact inferInstanceAs (Decidable False)
  | ok d => exact inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

theorem Tied.sound {k : Kore.Definition} (h : Tied k) : ∃ d, wf d = true ∧ KoreAML.Reordered d.emit k := by
  unfold Tied at h
  split at h
  · exact ⟨_, h⟩
  · exact h.elim

/-! ## The tie from its parts

A tie is checked in parts, each a decision of bounded size: `parse` (Parse.lean's stages), `wf`
conjunct by conjunct with the names' distinctness by codes (`KoreAML.Distinct`), and `Reordered`
from the user module's blocks compared with the KORE a slice at a time (`KoreAML.Blocks`). -/

theorem Tied.of_parts {k : Kore.Definition} {d : Definition} (hp : Parse.parse k = .ok d)
    (hw : wf d = true) (hr : KoreAML.Reordered d.emit k) : Tied k := by
  unfold Tied; rw [hp]; exact ⟨hw, hr⟩

theorem wf_of_parts {d : Definition} {p₁ p₂ : Nat}
    (hs : KoreAML.Distinct.codesDistinct p₁ (d.emit.sortDecls.map (·.name)) = true)
    (hy : KoreAML.Distinct.codesDistinct p₂ (d.emit.symbolDecls.map (·.name) ++ d.emit.aliasNames) = true)
    (hn : (d.sem.hooksApart && d.sem.predsApart && d.sem.idsOK) = true)
    (hok : d.sem.ok = true) (hc : d.cert.ok d.sem = true) (hpr : d.pres.ok d.sem = true)
    (hpa : d.paramsOK = true) (hfa : d.sem.faithOK = true) : wf d = true := by
  simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at hn
  simp only [wf, Definition.namesOK, KoreAML.Distinct.nodup_of_codes hs, KoreAML.Distinct.nodup_of_codes hy,
    hn.1.1, hn.1.2, hn.2, Semantics.okAll_of_ok hok, hc, hpr, hpa, hfa, Bool.and_self]

/-- `wf_of_parts` for a core outside `ok`, from `okAll`. -/
theorem wf_of_parts_all {d : Definition} {p₁ p₂ : Nat}
    (hs : KoreAML.Distinct.codesDistinct p₁ (d.emit.sortDecls.map (·.name)) = true)
    (hy : KoreAML.Distinct.codesDistinct p₂ (d.emit.symbolDecls.map (·.name) ++ d.emit.aliasNames) = true)
    (hn : (d.sem.hooksApart && d.sem.predsApart && d.sem.idsOK) = true)
    (hok : d.sem.okAll = true) (hc : d.cert.ok d.sem = true) (hpr : d.pres.ok d.sem = true)
    (hpa : d.paramsOK = true) (hfa : d.sem.faithOK = true) : wf d = true := by
  simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at hn
  simp only [wf, Definition.namesOK, KoreAML.Distinct.nodup_of_codes hs, KoreAML.Distinct.nodup_of_codes hy,
    hn.1.1, hn.1.2, hn.2, hok, hc, hpr, hpa, hfa, Bool.and_self]

/-- `Reordered d.emit k` from the user module's blocks: the prelude modules and the attributes
are the same, and the blocks are the KORE's segments in another order. -/
theorem reordered_of_blocks {d : Definition} {k : Kore.Definition} {mU : Kore.Module}
    {segs : List (List Kore.Sentence)} {n : Nat} {σ : List Nat}
    (hattr : d.emit.attributes = k.attributes)
    (hmods : k.modules = preludeModules ++ [mU])
    (hname : (userModule d.sem d.pres).name = mU.name)
    (hattrs : (userModule d.sem d.pres).attributes = mU.attributes)
    (hsents : mU.sentences = segs.flatten)
    (hlen : (userBlocks d.sem d.pres).length = n)
    (hslice : KoreAML.Blocks.SliceIs (userBlocks d.sem d.pres) segs 0 n σ)
    (hperm : σ.isPerm (List.range segs.length) = true) : KoreAML.Reordered d.emit k := by
  subst hlen
  have hp : (userModule d.sem d.pres).sentences.Perm mU.sentences := by
    have hu : (userModule d.sem d.pres).sentences = (userBlocks d.sem d.pres).flatten := by
      simp only [userModule]
    rw [hsents, hu]; exact KoreAML.Blocks.SliceIs.perm hslice hperm
  refine ⟨hattr, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [Definition.emit, emit, hmods, List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
  · intro mm hm
    simp only [Definition.emit, emit, hmods, List.zip_append rfl, List.mem_append, List.zip_cons_cons,
      List.zip_nil_left, List.mem_singleton] at hm
    rcases hm with hm | rfl
    · obtain ⟨i, hi, he⟩ := List.getElem_of_mem hm
      simp only [List.getElem_zip] at he
      subst he
      exact ⟨rfl, rfl, List.Perm.refl _⟩
    · exact ⟨hname, hattrs, hp⟩

end KCore

/-
  KCore. The conditions of `wf` (KCORE-SPEC.md §7). Reviewed layer, root track. Among them:
  - **subsorts** a strict partial order, given transitively closed as kompile writes it, over the
    user's sorts and the library's value sorts, every supersort a user sort; a sort may lie below
    several (`Int < AExp`, `Int < KResult`), and below a sort that is itself a subsort
    (`subsortsOK`);
  - not among them: that two equations of a function of one priority agree where both apply.
    `fnExclusiveOK` decides it where their patterns are apart (`overlapList`), their `requires` exclude each other
    (`reqsExclusive`: Bool literals, `==K` of different values, complementary or disjoint Int
    bounds, disjunctions) or their right-hand sides are one closed term (`clausesAgree`); the
    other functions are named obligations (`agreeObligations`). Two injections `inj{A,N}(p)`,
    `inj{B,N}(q)` overlap when A and B have a common lower bound, not only when they are
    comparable (`Int` below `AExp` and `KResult` makes `inj{AExp,KItem}(_)` and
    `inj{KResult,KItem}(_)` both match `inj{Int,KItem}(5)`), and then only if one of the injected
    patterns can itself denote an injection (`injable`); two collection patterns always overlap;
  - not among them: that two matches of one clause at one argument list give one result
    (`MatchIndependent`). `clauseFixed` decides it where the clause's patterns fix its variables;
    the other clauses are named obligations (`matchObligations`);
  - declarations and terms over the library's sorts with values (Set, the token sorts, the
    K-IO sorts) and its constructors; domain values of the token sorts;
  - the generated sort predicates callable in right-hand sides and `requires`;
  - rule and equation attributes: `owise` and `priority` are read into `Rule.prio` (Step.lean)
    and `Clause.prio` (Evaluation.lean); a priority without `priority{}("n")` is 50 or 200
    (`owise`);
  - the builtin library: the core's is the union of the imported modules' (`Presentation.ok`,
    Builtins.lean), with the facts the generic theorems read (`Lib.ok`).
-/
import KcoreSpec.Definition
import KcoreSpec.Value
import KcoreSpec.Builtins

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

def Fn.sig (f : Fn) : CtorSig := ⟨f.label, f.args, f.result⟩

def nodup {α : Type} [BEq α] : List α → Bool
  | [] => true
  | a :: as => !as.contains a && nodup as

def pairs {α : Type} : List α → List (α × α)
  | [] => []
  | a :: as => as.map (a, ·) ++ pairs as

/-! ## Terms -/

/-- Where a term occurs: a left-hand side (patterns: constructors, the map pattern symbols,
as-patterns), or a right-hand side / `requires` (constructors, hooks, functions). -/
structure TermCtx where
  lib : Lib
  subs : List (Srt × Srt)
  heads : List CtorSig
  asOK : Bool

mutual
  def sortOfTerm (x : TermCtx) (vs : List Srt) : Term → Option Srt
    | .var i => vs[i]?
    | .dv s lit => if dvOK x.lib s lit then some s else none
    | .app f ts => match lookupSig x.heads f with
      | some s => if sortsOfTerms x vs ts == some s.args then some s.result else none
      | none => none
    | .inj a b t => if x.subs.contains (a, b) && sortOfTerm x vs t == some a then some b else none
    | .as t i => match x.asOK, vs[i]?, sortOfTerm x vs t with
      | true, some v, some s => if v == s then some s else none
      | _, _, _ => none
    termination_by structural t => t
  def sortsOfTerms (x : TermCtx) (vs : List Srt) : List Term → Option (List Srt)
    | [] => some []
    | t :: ts => match sortOfTerm x vs t, sortsOfTerms x vs ts with
      | some s, some ss => some (s :: ss)
      | _, _ => none
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- A term's sort over some heads is its sort over more heads after them. -/
theorem lookupSig_append_some {l l' : List CtorSig} {f : Sym} {k : CtorSig} (h : lookupSig l f = some k) :
