    lookupSig (l ++ l') f = some k := by
  rw [lookupSig_eq] at h ⊢; rw [List.find?_append, h]; rfl

mutual
  theorem sortOfTerm_heads (x : TermCtx) (H : List CtorSig) (vs : List Srt) : ∀ (t : Term) {s : Srt},
      sortOfTerm x vs t = some s → sortOfTerm { x with heads := x.heads ++ H } vs t = some s
    | .var _, _, h => by simpa [sortOfTerm] using h
    | .dv _ _, _, h => by simpa [sortOfTerm] using h
    | .app f ts, s, h => by
      simp only [sortOfTerm] at h ⊢
      cases hk : lookupSig x.heads f with
      | none => rw [hk] at h; cases h
      | some k =>
        rw [hk] at h; rw [lookupSig_append_some hk]
        simp only at h ⊢
        by_cases he : (sortsOfTerms x vs ts == some k.args) = true
        · rw [if_pos he] at h
          rw [if_pos (by rw [sortsOfTerms_heads x H vs ts (beq_iff_eq.mp he)]; simp)]; exact h
        · rw [if_neg he] at h; cases h
    | .inj a b t, s, h => by
      simp only [sortOfTerm] at h ⊢
      by_cases hc : (x.subs.contains (a, b) && sortOfTerm x vs t == some a) = true
      · rw [if_pos hc] at h
        have hc' := hc
        simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at hc'
        have h2 := sortOfTerm_heads x H vs t hc'.2
        rw [if_pos (by simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq]; exact ⟨hc'.1, h2⟩)]; exact h
      · rw [if_neg hc] at h; cases h
    | .as t i, s, h => by
      simp only [sortOfTerm] at h ⊢
      cases ht : sortOfTerm x vs t with
      | none => rw [ht] at h; split at h <;> simp_all
      | some u => rw [ht] at h; rw [sortOfTerm_heads x H vs t ht]; exact h
  theorem sortsOfTerms_heads (x : TermCtx) (H : List CtorSig) (vs : List Srt) : ∀ (ts : List Term) {ss : List Srt},
      sortsOfTerms x vs ts = some ss → sortsOfTerms { x with heads := x.heads ++ H } vs ts = some ss
    | [], _, h => by simpa [sortsOfTerms] using h
    | t :: ts, ss, h => by
      simp only [sortsOfTerms] at h ⊢
      cases h1 : sortOfTerm x vs t with
      | none => rw [h1] at h; cases h
      | some a =>
        cases h2 : sortsOfTerms x vs ts with
        | none => rw [h1, h2] at h; cases h
        | some b => rw [h1, h2] at h; rw [sortOfTerm_heads x H vs t h1, sortsOfTerms_heads x H vs ts h2]; exact h
end

mutual
  def varOccs : Term → List Nat
    | .var i => [i]
    | .app _ ts => varOccsList ts
    | .inj _ _ t => varOccs t
    | .as t i => varOccs t ++ [i]
    | .dv _ _ => []
    termination_by structural t => t
  def varOccsList : List Term → List Nat
    | [] => []
    | t :: ts => varOccs t ++ varOccsList ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

def linearCover (n : Nat) (occs : List Nat) : Bool :=
  occs.length == n && (List.range n).all occs.contains

/-- Every variable `0, …, n-1` occurs (repetitions allowed). -/
def binds (n : Nat) (occs : List Nat) : Bool := (List.range n).all occs.contains

mutual
  /-- A map pattern: `_Map_` trees of `k |-> v` (any patterns), `.Map`, and variables; the result
  counts the variables at map positions (frames). -/
  def mapFrames : Term → Option Nat
    | .app f ts => mapFramesApp f ts
    | .var _ => some 1
    | _ => none
    termination_by structural t => t
  def mapFramesApp (f : Sym) : List Term → Option Nat
    | [a, b] => if f == mapConcat then
        match mapFrames a, mapFrames b with
        | some m, some n => some (m + n)
        | _, _ => none
      else if f == mapElem then (if noMapIn a && noMapIn b then some 0 else none) else none
    | [] => if f == mapUnit then some 0 else none
    | _ => none
    termination_by structural ts => ts
  /-- A pattern outside map positions: every map subpattern has at most one frame. -/
  def noMapIn : Term → Bool
    | .app f ts => if patternHooks.contains f then (match mapFramesApp f ts with
        | some n => n ≤ 1
        | none => false) else noMapInList ts
    | .inj _ _ t => noMapIn t
    | .as t _ => noMapIn t
    | .var _ => true
    | .dv _ _ => true
    termination_by structural t => t
  def noMapInList : List Term → Bool
    | [] => true
    | t :: ts => noMapIn t && noMapInList ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

mutual
  /-- No map pattern symbol at all (function clauses). -/
  def mapFree : Term → Bool
    | .app f ts => !patternHooks.contains f && mapFreeList ts
    | .inj _ _ t => mapFree t
    | .as t _ => mapFree t
    | _ => true
    termination_by structural t => t
  def mapFreeList : List Term → Bool
    | [] => true
    | t :: ts => mapFree t && mapFreeList ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

def peelAs : Term → Term
  | .as t _ => peelAs t
  | t => t

/-- Whether a pattern can denote an injection: a variable, an injection, or an alias of one. A
literal denotes a domain value, a constructor its constructor term, and the map, list and
cell-map symbols a collection (`PatVal`): none of them an injection. -/
def injable (t : Term) : Bool :=
  match peelAs t with
  | .var _ => true
  | .inj .. => true
  | _ => false

/-- The library's collection symbols: the unit, element and concatenation of maps, sets and lists. -/
def collHooks : List Sym := patternHooks ++ [setUnit, setElem, setConcat] ++ listPatternHooks

mutual
  /-- `false` only if no value matches both patterns (distinct literals apart).
  `meet a b`: the sorts a and b have a common lower bound (one of them, or a third sort below
  both), so injections from them can denote the same value. Two injections `inj{a,N}(p)` and
  `inj{b,N}(q)` with a ≠ b denote one value `inj{a',N}(v)` only from a sort a' below both
  (`injNormal`); a' differs from a or from b, and there p or q denotes the injection
  `inj{a',a}(v)` or `inj{a',b}(v)`, so one of them must be able to denote an injection
  (`injable`): `inj{ExceptionalStatusCode,StatusCode}(EVMC_FAILURE)` and
  `inj{EndStatusCode,StatusCode}(EVMC_SUCCESS)` are apart.
  `coll f`: f is a collection symbol (`Semantics.collHead`). Two patterns headed by collection
  symbols overlap whatever their heads and arguments: a collection is the same value however it is
  built, so `.Map` and `M N`, or `1 |-> A M` and `2 |-> B N`, denote one map. Constructor terms and
  collections are different values. -/
  def overlap (meet : Srt → Srt → Bool) (coll : Sym → Bool) : Term → Term → Bool
    | .var _, _ => true
    | .as p _, q => overlap meet coll p q
    | .dv s l, q => match peelAs q with
      | .var _ => true
      | .dv s' l' => s == s' && l == l'
      | _ => false
    | .app f ps, q => match peelAs q with
      | .var _ => true
      | .app g qs => (coll f && coll g) || (f == g && overlapList meet coll ps qs)
      | _ => false
    | .inj a _ p, q => match peelAs q with
      | .var _ => true
      | .inj b _ q' => if a == b then overlap meet coll p q' else meet a b && (injable p || injable q')
      | _ => false
    termination_by structural p => p
  def overlapList (meet : Srt → Srt → Bool) (coll : Sym → Bool) : List Term → List Term → Bool
    | p :: ps, q :: qs => overlap meet coll p q && overlapList meet coll ps qs
    | _, _ => true
    termination_by structural ps => ps
end

/-! ## Syntactic facts the function conditions read (moved from Determinism.lean, 2026-11-09:
the clause conditions of `fnOK` call them; DetSound.lean and Uniq.lean prove what they mean) -/

/-- The literals a `requires` equal to `true` asserts: each conjunct of `_andBool_`, `notBool A`
as `A = false`, `true` none, anything else `A = true`. -/
def lits : Term → List (Term × Bool)
  | .app f [t₁, t₂] => if f == boolAnd then lits t₁ ++ lits t₂ else [(.app f [t₁, t₂], true)]
  | .app f [t] => if f == boolNot then [(t, false)] else [(.app f [t], true)]
  | .dv s l => if s == Srt.bool && l == .bool true then [] else [(.dv s l, true)]
  | t => [(t, true)]

mutual
  def Term.beq : Term → Term → Bool
    | .var i, .var j => i == j
    | .app f ts, .app g us => f == g && Term.beqList ts us
    | .inj a b t, .inj a' b' t' => a == a' && b == b' && Term.beq t t'
    | .as t i, .as t' j => i == j && Term.beq t t'
    | .dv s l, .dv s' l' => s == s' && l == l'
    | _, _ => false
    termination_by structural t => t
  def Term.beqList : List Term → List Term → Bool
    | [], [] => true
    | t :: ts, u :: us => Term.beq t u && Term.beqList ts us
    | _, _ => false
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-! `uniq c D p`: the variables a match of p fixes, given those of D (`f` is a constructor of c
when `lookupSig c.ctorSigs f` finds it, `Semantics.isCtor`). -/

mutual
  /-- `some D'`: two well-sorted σ, σ' under which p denotes one value, and that agree on D,
  agree on D'. -/
  def uniq (c : Semantics) (D : List Nat) : Term → Option (List Nat)
    | .var i => some (i :: D)
    | .dv _ _ => some D
    | .inj _ _ p => uniq c D p
    | .as p i => (uniq c D p).map (i :: ·)
    | .app f ps =>
      if (lookupSig c.ctorSigs f).isSome then uniqList c D ps
      else if f == mapUnit then (if ps.isEmpty then some D else none)
      else if f == mapConcat then uniqConcat c D ps
      else none
    termination_by structural p => p
  def uniqList (c : Semantics) (D : List Nat) : List Term → Option (List Nat)
    | [] => some D
    | p :: ps => (uniq c D p).bind fun D' => uniqList c D' ps
    termination_by structural ps => ps
  /-- `K |-> V M`, the key's variables in D: V's value, then M's, are fixed. -/
  def uniqConcat (c : Semantics) (D : List Nat) : List Term → Option (List Nat)
    | [.app e [k, v], rest] =>
      if e == mapElem && (varOccs k).all D.contains then (uniq c D v).bind fun D' => uniq c D' rest
      else none
    | _ => none
    termination_by structural ps => ps
end

/-! ## Coverage -/

/-- A generator of a sort: a constructor, or the injection from a direct subsort. -/
inductive Gen where
  | ctor (c : CtorSig)
  | inj (src : Srt)
  deriving Repr

def Gen.argSorts : Gen → List Srt
  | .ctor c => c.args
  | .inj a => [a]

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

def gens (N : Srt) : List Gen :=
  (c.ctorSigs.filter (·.result == N)).map .ctor ++
  (sortBy id ((c.subsorts.filter (·.2 == N)).map (·.1))).map .inj

/-- The sorts whose generators `covers` enumerates: those whose values are exactly the applications
of their generators (`gens`: constructor terms of the sort, and injections from its subsorts). A
user sort is one, unless it is a collection sort (`collOf`: its values are collections, which no
generator builds) or holds domain values (Int, Bool, KConfigVar, the library's token and byte sorts:
its literals, `dvOK`). Base sorts, K, KItem and those sorts are covered only by variables. -/
def enumerable (N : Srt) : Bool :=
  c.userSorts.contains N && (c.collOf N).isNone &&
    !(N == Srt.int || N == Srt.bool || N == Srt.kconfigVar || c.lib.tokenSorts.contains N ||
      c.lib.byteSorts.contains N)

/-- a and b have a common lower bound. -/
def meet (a b : Srt) : Bool :=
  c.le a b || c.le b a || c.subsorts.any fun (s, _) => c.le s a && c.le s b

/-- A collection symbol: one of the library's (`collHooks`), or a parameter implemented by one (a
collection sort's unit, element and concatenation, `collOK`). -/
def collHead (f : Sym) : Bool :=
  collHooks.contains f || c.params.any fun k => k.sig.name == f && (k.impl.map collHooks.contains).getD false

end Semantics

/-- Row `ps` specialised to generator `g`: `none` if its head pattern cannot match a `g` value. -/
def specialize (g : Gen) : List Term → Option (List Term)
  | [] => none
  | p :: ps => match peelAs p, g with
    | .var _, g => some ((g.argSorts.map fun _ => Term.var 0) ++ ps)
    | .app f qs, .ctor k => if f == k.name then some (qs ++ ps) else none
    | .inj a _ q, .inj a' => if a == a' then some (q :: ps) else none
    | _, _ => none

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- Every well-sorted vector of values of the sorts `ss` matches some row (the classic
usefulness check, without `requires`). Fuel bounds the recursion; running out answers `false`,
so the check can only reject more. -/
def covers : Nat → List Srt → List (List Term) → Bool
  | 0, _, _ => false
  | _ + 1, [], rows => !rows.isEmpty
  | n + 1, s :: ss, rows =>
    let varRows := rows.filterMap fun r => match r with
      | p :: ps => (match peelAs p with | .var _ => some ps | _ => none)
      | [] => none
    if c.enumerable s && varRows.length != rows.length then
      (c.gens s).all fun g => covers n (g.argSorts ++ ss) (rows.filterMap (specialize g))
    else covers n ss varRows

/-! ## Declarations, cells, functions, rules -/

end Semantics

def reqOK (x : TermCtx) (vs : List Srt) : Option Term → Bool
  | none => true
  | some t => sortOfTerm x vs t == some Srt.bool

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- The library's sorts whose elements are all values: all but Float and MInt, of which KCore
represents no value (a List is the sequence of its elements, `GroundTerm.list`). -/
def libValueSorts : List Srt :=
  c.lib.sortsBelowKItem.filter fun s => ![Srt.float].contains s

/-- The library's sorts with generators: constructors (K-IO's) or injections from library sorts. -/
def libCtorSorts : List Srt :=
  c.lib.sortsBelowKItem.filter fun s => c.lib.ctors.any (·.result == s) || c.lib.subsorts.any (·.2 == s)

/-- The library's sorts whose values are constructor terms: those with generators
(`libCtorSorts`) that hold no domain value (Int, Bool, KConfigVar, the library's token and byte
sorts, whose values are their literals, `dvOK`) and are no collection sort (`collOf`, whose values
are collections). JSON is one (`null`, `JSONEntry`, …, and injections); Int and Map are not. -/
def libConsSorts : List Srt :=
  c.libCtorSorts.filter fun s => s != Srt.int && s != Srt.bool && s != Srt.kconfigVar &&
    !c.lib.tokenSorts.contains s && !c.lib.byteSorts.contains s && (c.collOf s).isNone

/-- A declared argument sort: one of the definition's sorts (a cell sort among them: KEVM's `{_|_}`
of `Accounts` takes two cells, `getTxData` the top cell), K, KItem, a library sort with values, or
Int, whose values are its literals whatever the library (`dvOK`; the counter cell holds one). -/
def argSortOK (s : Srt) : Bool :=
  c.userSorts.contains s || [Srt.k, Srt.kitem, Srt.int].contains s || c.libValueSorts.contains s

def resultSortOK (s : Srt) : Bool :=
  c.userSorts.contains s || s == Srt.kitem || c.libValueSorts.contains s

def declsOK : Bool :=
  (c.ctors.all fun k => k.args.all c.argSortOK && (c.userSorts.contains k.result || k.result == Srt.kitem)) &&
  (c.fns.all fun f => f.args.all c.argSortOK && c.resultSortOK f.result) &&
  (c.userSorts.contains c.pgmSort || [Srt.k, Srt.kitem, Srt.int, Srt.bool].contains c.pgmSort)

mutual
  def cellNames : Cell → List String
    | .leaf n _ _ => [n]
    | .node n cs _ => n :: cellNamesList cs
    termination_by structural x => x
  def cellNamesList : List Cell → List String
    | [] => []
    | x :: xs => cellNames x ++ cellNamesList xs
    termination_by structural xs => xs
  def cellLeaves : Cell → List (String × Srt)
    | .leaf n s _ => [(n, s)]
    | .node _ cs _ => cellLeavesList cs
    termination_by structural x => x
  def cellLeavesList : List Cell → List (String × Srt)
    | [] => []
    | x :: xs => cellLeaves x ++ cellLeavesList xs
    termination_by structural xs => xs
end

mutual
  /-- A user cell has the sorts and symbols of its kind: its `Opt` sort and `noXCell`, and for a
  node its fragment sort and `<x>-fragment`, which a leaf has not; and so have its children. -/
  def cellIdsShaped : Cell → Bool
    | .leaf _ _ i => i.opt.isSome && i.no.isSome && i.frag.isNone && i.fragLabel.isNone
    | .node _ cs i =>
      i.opt.isSome && i.no.isSome && i.frag.isSome && i.fragLabel.isSome && cellIdsShapedList cs
    termination_by structural x => x
  def cellIdsShapedList : List Cell → Bool
    | [] => true
    | x :: xs => cellIdsShaped x && cellIdsShapedList xs
    termination_by structural xs => xs
end

def alnum (n : String) : Bool := !n.isEmpty && n.toList.all Char.isAlphanum

/-- A cell name: letters, digits and inner dashes (`exit-code`, whose sort is `ExitCodeCell`). The
names derived from it are told apart by `namesOK`. -/
def cellNameOK (n : String) : Bool :=
  !n.isEmpty && n.toList.all (fun ch => ch.isAlphanum || ch == '-') && n.toList.head? != some '-'

/-- The declared subsorts form a strict partial order into sorts whose values are constructor
terms: each declared pair `a < b` has a lower sort a that is a user sort or a library sort with
values, and an upper sort b that is a user sort or a library sort whose values are constructor
terms (`libConsSorts`: KEVM's `Account < JSON`); the closure (`declaredClosure`) is irreflexive, so
there is no cycle; the pairs are declared once. A value of b is a constructor or an injection
applied to values, and `inj{a,b}(v)` is one of b's generators (`gens`) whichever module declares b:
the injection is read like the library's own. A sort of domain values or a collection sort is no
upper sort: its values are its literals or collections, and an injected value there would be one
no hook is defined on. A sort may lie below several sorts and chains may be long (KCORE-SPEC.md
Q24): values stay unique because an injection is never nested (`sortOf`), so a value of sort b
holding a value of sort a is `inj{a,b}(v)` with v not an injection, through any chain. -/
def subsortsOK : Bool :=
  let subs := c.userSubsorts
  subs.all (fun (a, b) => a != b && (c.userSorts.contains a || c.libValueSorts.contains a) &&
    (c.userSorts.contains b || c.libConsSorts.contains b)) &&
  c.declaredClosure.all (fun (a, b) => a != b) &&
  nodup subs

/-- The library's facts the generic theorems read (NamesApart.lean): its sorts below KItem are
registry sorts other than KItem and the generated cells', each once; its subsorts relate them; no
constructor of it is a map-pattern symbol. Every union of the library's modules has them; they
are checked on the definition's. -/
def _root_.KCore.Lib.ok (l : Lib) : Bool :=
  l.sortsBelowKItem.all (fun s => decide (s < nRegSorts) && !(17 ≤ s && s ≤ 20) && s != Srt.kitem) &&
  nodup l.sortsBelowKItem &&
  l.subsorts.all (fun p => l.sortsBelowKItem.contains p.1 && l.sortsBelowKItem.contains p.2) &&
  l.ctors.all (fun k => !patternHooks.contains k.name)

/-- The definition's own sorts and symbols are numbered as Core.lean says: its own sorts
(`ownSorts`) are `nRegSorts, nRegSorts + 1, …`, one name each; its symbols but the sort predicates
(`ownSyms`) are `symBase, symBase + 1, …`, one name each, after the predicates of its own sorts.
So all of them are distinct, from each other and from the registry's, and `predOf` gives each own
sort its own predicate. Linear in their number. Its other sorts are the registry's generated
configuration sorts (`genSorts`), each once, and its other constructors the generated
configuration's (`genSyms`); no library sort is one of them, nor KItem (`Lib.ok`). -/
def idsOK : Bool :=
  c.ownSorts == List.range' nRegSorts c.sortNames.length &&
  c.ownSyms == List.range' c.symBase (c.symNames.length - c.sortNames.length) &&
  decide (c.sortNames.length ≤ c.symNames.length) &&
  ((let reg := c.userSorts.filter fun s => decide (s < nRegSorts)
    nodup reg && reg.all genSorts.contains &&
    c.ctors.all fun k => decide (nRegSyms ≤ k.name) || genSyms.contains k.name) && c.lib.ok)

/-- Every sort of the definition has a value: the least set of sorts closed under generators whose
argument sorts it holds (constructors and injections), from K, KItem, Int, the library's value
sorts and the definition's collection sorts (each has its empty collection), holds every one of
`userSorts`. -/
def inhabited : Bool :=
  let univ := c.userSorts
  let step := fun (inh : List Srt) =>
    inh ++ univ.filter fun N =>
      !inh.contains N && (c.gens N).any fun g => g.argSorts.all inh.contains
  let all := Nat.repeat step univ.length ([Srt.k, Srt.kitem, Srt.int] ++ c.libValueSorts ++ c.colls.map (·.sort))
  c.userSorts.all all.contains

def patCtx : TermCtx := ⟨c.lib, c.subsorts, c.ctorSigs ++ hookSigs.filter (patternHooks.contains ·.name), true⟩

/-- The collection pattern symbols' signatures (`PatVal.coll`): the library's list symbols, and the
parameters implemented by a map or list pattern symbol (a cell map's). -/
def collPatSigs : List CtorSig :=
  hookSigs.filter (collPatternHooks.contains ·.name) ++
    (c.params.filter fun k => match k.impl with
      | some g => patternHooks.contains g || listPatternHooks.contains g
      | none => false).map (·.sig)

/-- The well-formedness context of a rule's left-hand side: the matcher's (`patCtx`), then the
collection pattern symbols. -/
def patCtxAll : TermCtx := { c.patCtx with heads := c.patCtx.heads ++ c.collPatSigs }
/-- Right-hand sides and `requires`: constructors, hooks, the parameter symbols, the generated
sort predicates and the functions given. -/
def rhsCtx (fns : List CtorSig) : TermCtx :=
  ⟨c.lib, c.subsorts, c.ctorSigs ++ hookSigs ++ c.params.map (·.sig) ++ c.sortPreds.map Fn.sig ++ fns, false⟩

/-- The clause's match fixes every variable: two well-sorted substitutions under which its
patterns denote one list of arguments agree on all of its variables (`uniqList`). A map pattern
`K |-> V M` is allowed where its key's variables are fixed by the arguments before it, since a
map's keys are unique: kimp's `<env>` lookup, and `lev(X:Id, X |-> L _)` in a function. So a
clause has at most one instance at given arguments, and it is match independent
(`clauseFixed_sound`). It is not a condition of `clauseOK`: the clauses it does not confirm are
named obligations (`matchObligations`), and the executable evaluation's completeness reads it of
every clause (`clausesFixed`). -/
def clauseFixed (cl : Clause) : Bool :=
  match uniqList c [] cl.pats with
  | some D => (List.range cl.vars.length).all D.contains
  | none => false

/-- Well-sorted patterns of the argument sorts, each map pattern with at most one frame
(`noMapIn`), binding every variable (repetitions allowed: a key bound in one argument and looked
up in a map in a later one); a Bool `requires` and a right-hand side of the result sort. That the
match fixes the variables is not checked here (`clauseFixed`, `matchObligations`). -/
def clauseOK (f : Fn) (rhsHeads : List CtorSig) (cl : Clause) : Bool :=
  sortsOfTerms c.patCtx cl.vars cl.pats == some f.args &&
  noMapInList cl.pats &&
  binds cl.vars.length (varOccsList cl.pats) &&
  reqOK (c.rhsCtx rhsHeads) cl.vars cl.req &&
  sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx rhsHeads) cl.vars cl.rhs == some f.result

def coverFuel (f : Fn) : Nat := 1000 * (f.clauses.length + 1)

end Semantics

mutual
  def callsOf (f : Sym) : Term → List (List Term)
    | .app g ts => (if g == f then [ts] else []) ++ callsOfList f ts
    | .inj _ _ t => callsOf f t
    | .as t _ => callsOf f t
    | _ => []
    termination_by structural t => t
  def callsOfList (f : Sym) : List Term → List (List Term)
    | [] => []
    | t :: ts => callsOf f t ++ callsOfList f ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- A constructor of `c` that is no map pattern symbol: an application of it in a pattern denotes
only the constructor term (`PatVal.ctor`; `PatVal.hook` reads the map pattern symbols,
`PatVal.coll` symbols that are no constructor). -/
def Semantics.ctorPat (c : Semantics) (g : Sym) : Bool :=
  (lookupSig c.ctorSigs g).isSome && !patternHooks.contains g

mutual
  /-- The variable `j` occurs in the pattern on a path of applications of symbols `pat` admits,
  injections and aliases only. -/
  def ctorPathIn (pat : Sym → Bool) (j : Nat) : Term → Bool
    | .var i => i == j
    | .app g ts => pat g && ctorPathInList pat j ts
    | .inj _ _ t => ctorPathIn pat j t
    | .as t _ => ctorPathIn pat j t
    | .dv _ _ => false
    termination_by structural t => t
  def ctorPathInList (pat : Sym → Bool) (j : Nat) : List Term → Bool
    | [] => false
    | t :: ts => ctorPathIn pat j t || ctorPathInList pat j ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- The variable `j` lies strictly inside the pattern: under at least one application of a symbol
`pat` admits, on a path of such applications, injections and aliases only (`ctorPathIn`). With
`pat` the constructors that are no map pattern symbol (`Semantics.ctorPat`), a value the pattern
denotes is strictly larger than j's (`GroundTerm.size`, `strictlyIn_size` in Terminates.lean): on
such an application only the constructor case of `PatVal` applies, a constructor value is strictly
larger than each argument, and injections and aliases do not shrink a value. A collection pattern
gives no such bound: a frame variable can denote the whole value (`_Map_(.Map, M)`,
`_List_(L₁, L₂)` with L₁ empty). -/
def strictlyIn (pat : Sym → Bool) (j : Nat) : Term → Bool
  | .app g ts => pat g && ctorPathInList pat j ts
  | .inj _ _ t => strictlyIn pat j t
  | .as t _ => strictlyIn pat j t
  | _ => false

/-- The self calls of `f`, each with the patterns of the clause it is in: in the right-hand sides
and the `requires`. -/
def selfCalls (f : Fn) : List (List Term × List Term) :=
  f.clauses.flatMap fun cl =>
    (callsOf f.label cl.rhs ++ (cl.req.map (callsOf f.label)).getD []).map (cl.pats, ·)

/-- Self calls decrease at `dec`, in the right-hand side and in the `requires`: the argument at
`dec` is a variable strictly inside the clause's pattern there (`strictlyIn`). -/
def decreasingOK (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (dec : Option Nat) : Bool :=
  let calls := selfCalls f
  calls.isEmpty || match dec with
    | none => false
    | some i => calls.all fun (pats, args) => match args[i]?, pats[i]? with
      | some (.var j), some p => strictlyIn c.ctorPat j p
      | _, _ => false

namespace Semantics
variable (c : Semantics)

/-- The sorts whose values the interpreted symbols take apart: Int, Bool, Map, Set and List. -/
def _root_.KCore.shapeSorts : List Srt := [Srt.int, Srt.bool, Srt.map, Srt.set, Srt.list]

/-- Every value of a sort of `shapeSorts` is a domain value or a collection of that sort: no
constructor, injection, token or byte sort, nor collection sort of the definition's own, has one
of them as its sort. Then an Int is an Int literal, a Map a map, and so on, which the interpreted
symbols read. -/
def shapesOK : Bool :=
  c.ctorSigs.all (fun k => !shapeSorts.contains k.result) &&
  c.subsorts.all (fun p => !shapeSorts.contains p.2) &&
  !(c.lib.tokenSorts ++ c.lib.byteSorts).any shapeSorts.contains &&
  c.colls.all (fun k => !shapeSorts.contains k.sort)

mutual
  /-- A term whose value is defined wherever its variables have values: variables, domain values,
  injections, constructors, the interpreted symbols that are total (all but `partialHooks`), and
  calls of the functions named in `tot` that are no interpreted symbol and no parameter symbol (an
  application of one of those has its value, `EvalTerm.hook`, `EvalTerm.param`, whatever function
  bears its number, and it may be undefined). -/
  def totalTerm (tot : List Sym) : Term → Bool
    | .var _ => true
    | .dv _ _ => true
    | .inj _ _ t => totalTerm tot t
    | .as _ _ => false
    | .app f ts =>
      ((lookupSig c.ctorSigs f).isSome || (hookSigs.any (·.name == f) && !partialHooks.contains f) ||
        (tot.contains f && !hookSigs.any (·.name == f) && !c.params.any (·.sig.name == f))) &&
        totalTermList tot ts
    termination_by structural t => t
  def totalTermList (tot : List Sym) : List Term → Bool
    | [] => true
    | t :: ts => totalTerm tot t && totalTermList tot ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- The functions declared total before f. -/
def totalBefore (f : Fn) : List Sym :=
  ((c.fns.takeWhile (·.label != f.label)).filter (·.total)).map (·.label)

/-- The rows of a clause in `covers`: its patterns, when it has no `requires` and its pattern
variables occur at most once across the row. A row with a repeated variable matches only arguments
equal at those positions, so reading it as independent variables overstates what it covers. -/
def coverRows (f : Fn) : List (List Term) :=
  (f.clauses.filter fun cl => cl.req.isNone && nodup (varOccsList cl.pats)).map (·.pats)

/-- The first argument at which f's self calls decrease (`decreasingOK`), if any; `none` (no self
call allowed) when there is none. -/
def decArg (f : Fn) : Option Nat :=
  (List.range f.args.length).find? fun i => decreasingOK c f (some i)

/-- A function declared `[total]` is defined at every argument of its sorts: the values of the
sorts the interpreted symbols read have their shapes (`shapesOK`, so the hooks but `partialHooks`
are defined at values of their sorts); its self calls decrease (`decreasingOK` at `decArg`); its
covering rows (`coverRows`, of every priority) cover its argument sorts; and every right-hand side
is total over the total functions before it, the sort predicates and itself (`total_of_totalOK`,
Totals.lean). Then the functional axiom kompile writes for it, `∃y. f(x̄) = y`, holds where
evaluation gives its value. The total functions before it are the well-founded order of the
argument. A `[total]` declaration this check cannot confirm is listed in `totalObligations`: under
the reading of partial functions (§2.5), its axiom could be false. -/
def totalOK (f : Fn) : Bool :=
  let tot := c.totalBefore f ++ c.sortPreds.map (·.label) ++ [f.label]
  c.shapesOK && decreasingOK c f (c.decArg f) &&
  c.covers (coverFuel f) f.args (coverRows f) &&
  f.clauses.all (fun cl => c.totalTerm tot cl.rhs)

/-- `t ==K u` as a literal asserted true. -/
def eqKLit : Term × Bool → Option (Term × Term)
  | (.app f [t, u], true) => if f == kEq then some (t, u) else none
  | _ => none

mutual
  /-- A ground term of constructors, domain values and injections, no injection directly over
  another: its value is the term itself read as a value, so two such terms that differ have
  different values. -/
  def groundValue : Term → Bool
    | .dv _ _ => true
    | .app f ts => (lookupSig c.ctorSigs f).isSome && groundValueList ts
    | .inj _ _ t => (match t with | .inj .. => false | _ => true) && groundValue t
    | _ => false
    termination_by structural t => t
  def groundValueList : List Term → Bool
    | [] => true
    | t :: ts => groundValue t && groundValueList ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- Two Int comparisons that are each other's negation on every pair of Ints. -/
def intCompl : List (Sym × Sym) :=
  [(intLt, intGe), (intGe, intLt), (intLe, intGt), (intGt, intLe), (intEq, intNe), (intNe, intEq)]

/-- `x op y` and `x op' y` with `op'` the complement of `op` (`intCompl`), asserted alike. -/
def complLits (x : TermCtx) (vs : List Srt) : Term × Bool → Term × Bool → Bool
  | (.app f [t, u], b), (.app g [t', u'], b') =>
      intCompl.contains (f, g) && Term.beq t t' && Term.beq u u' && b == b' &&
        (sortOfTerm x vs t).isSome && (sortOfTerm x vs u).isSome
  | _, _ => false

/-- The value of an Int literal term. -/
def intLitOf : Term → Option Int
  | .dv s (.int k) => if s == Srt.int then some k else none
  | _ => none

/-- The bounds `x op k` asserts of the Int x, for an Int comparison op asserted `true`
(`lo ≤ x ≤ hi`, each bound optional; `=/=Int` none). -/
def cmpBound (f : Sym) (k : Int) : Option (Option Int × Option Int) :=
  if f == intLt then some (none, some (k - 1))
  else if f == intLe then some (none, some k)
  else if f == intGt then some (some (k + 1), none)
  else if f == intGe then some (some k, none)
  else if f == intEq then some (some k, some k)
  else none

/-- The comparison asserted: `op` itself when asserted `true`, its complement (`intCompl`) when
`false`. -/
def cmpAsserted (f : Sym) (b : Bool) : Option Sym :=
  if f == intLt then some (if b then intLt else intGe)
  else if f == intGe then some (if b then intGe else intLt)
  else if f == intLe then some (if b then intLe else intGt)
  else if f == intGt then some (if b then intGt else intLe)
  else if f == intEq then some (if b then intEq else intNe)
  else if f == intNe then some (if b then intNe else intEq)
  else none

/-- `k op x` read as `x op' k`. -/
def cmpFlip (f : Sym) : Option Sym :=
  if f == intLt then some intGt else if f == intLe then some intGe
  else if f == intGt then some intLt else if f == intGe then some intLe
  else if f == intEq then some intEq else if f == intNe then some intNe else none

/-- A literal comparing an Int term with an Int literal, as the term and the bounds it puts on
the term's value: `x op k`, or `k op x`, asserted `b`. -/
def intBound : Term × Bool → Option (Term × Option Int × Option Int)
  | (.app f [x, y], b) =>
    match cmpAsserted f b with
    | none => none
    | some g =>
      match intLitOf y with
      | some k => (cmpBound g k).map fun r => (x, r)
      | none =>
        match intLitOf x, cmpFlip g with
        | some k, some g' => (cmpBound g' k).map fun r => (y, r)
        | _, _ => none
  | _ => none

/-- Two bounded ranges with nothing in common: one's lower bound above the other's upper. -/
def boundsApart : Option Int × Option Int → Option Int × Option Int → Bool
  | (lo, hi), (lo', hi') =>
    (match lo, hi' with | some l, some h => decide (h < l) | _, _ => false) ||
    (match lo', hi with | some l, some h => decide (h < l) | _, _ => false)

/-- Two literals never both hold under one substitution (`reqsExclusive`'s cases): a Bool
literal negated; `t ==K a` and `t ==K b` with a, b different ground values; complementary
comparisons of the same Ints (`complLits`); or bounds on one Int term by Int literals with no
value in common (`intBound`: `I <Int 0` and `0 <=Int I`, `sgn(I) ==Int -1` and
`sgn(I) ==Int 1`). -/
def litsApart (heads : List CtorSig) (vs : List Srt) : Term × Bool → Term × Bool → Bool
  | (A, b), (A', b') =>
      (Term.beq A A' && b != b' && sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx heads) vs A == some Srt.bool) ||
      (match eqKLit (A, b), eqKLit (A', b') with
       | some (x, a), some (x', a') => Term.beq x x' && (sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx heads) vs x).isSome &&
           c.groundValue a && c.groundValue a' && !Term.beq a a'
       | _, _ => false) ||
      complLits (c.rhsCtx heads) vs (A, b) (A', b') ||
      (match intBound (A, b), intBound (A', b') with
       | some (x, r), some (x', r') => Term.beq x x' && (sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx heads) vs x).isSome &&
           boundsApart r r'
       | _, _ => false)

/-- A literal of one `requires` that the other's literals exclude: some literal apart from it,
or, for a disjunction `A orBool B` asserted `true`, both disjuncts excluded. -/
def litExcluded (heads : List CtorSig) (vs : List Srt) (ls' : List (Term × Bool)) : Term × Bool → Bool
  | (.app f [A₁, A₂], true) =>
    if f == boolOr then
      ls'.any (c.litsApart heads vs (A₁, true)) && ls'.any (c.litsApart heads vs (A₂, true))
    else ls'.any (c.litsApart heads vs (.app f [A₁, A₂], true))
  | l => ls'.any (c.litsApart heads vs l)

/-- Two `requires` over the variables `vs` that are never both `true` under one substitution:
a literal of one excluded by the other's (`litExcluded`, `litsApart`). -/
def reqsExclusive (heads : List CtorSig) (vs : List Srt) : Option Term → Option Term → Bool
  | some q, some q' => (lits q).any (c.litExcluded heads vs (lits q'))
  | _, _ => false

/-- Two clauses whose patterns may match one argument list, with one variable list and one pattern
list and `requires` that exclude each other: then at most one applies at any arguments. -/
def clausesExclusive (heads : List CtorSig) (cl cl' : Clause) : Bool :=
  cl.vars == cl'.vars && Term.beqList cl.pats cl'.pats && c.reqsExclusive heads cl.vars cl.req cl'.req

/-- Two clauses whose right-hand sides are one term without variables: wherever both apply, they
are the same instance of one right-hand side. -/
def _root_.KCore.clausesAgree (cl cl' : Clause) : Bool :=
  Term.beq cl.rhs cl'.rhs && (varOccs cl.rhs).isEmpty

mutual
  /-- The symbols a term applies. -/
  def _root_.KCore.Term.heads : Term → List Sym
    | .app f ts => f :: Term.headsList ts
    | .inj _ _ t => Term.heads t
    | .as t _ => Term.heads t
    | _ => []
    termination_by structural t => t
  def _root_.KCore.Term.headsList : List Term → List Sym
    | [] => []
    | t :: ts => Term.heads t ++ Term.headsList ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- The symbols a function's right-hand sides and `requires` apply. -/
def _root_.KCore.Fn.callees (f : Fn) : List Sym :=
  f.clauses.flatMap fun cl => Term.heads cl.rhs ++ (cl.req.map Term.heads).getD []

/-- The symbols some rule's right-hand side or `requires`, or some function, applies. -/
def appliedSyms : List Sym :=
  c.rules.flatMap (fun r => Term.heads r.rhs ++ (r.req.map Term.heads).getD []) ++
  c.fns.flatMap (·.callees)

/-- The functions that call a function declared after them. Declaration order, with decreasing
self calls (`Certificates.ok`), is KCore's argument that evaluation terminates
(`terminates_of_order`, Terminates.lean); for these functions it does not apply, and their
termination is a named obligation (`Obligations`, Statements.lean). -/
def orderObligations : List Sym :=
  let labels := c.fns.map (·.label)
  let rec go (earlier : List Sym) : List Fn → List Sym
    | [] => []
    | f :: fs =>
      (if f.callees.all (fun g => g == f.label || earlier.contains g || !labels.contains g) then []
       else [f.label]) ++ go (earlier ++ [f.label]) fs
  go [] c.fns

/-- Well-formed clauses over constructors, hooks and the functions `heads` (`fnsOK`: every
function of the definition, in any order: functions may call one another, mutually recursively,
since `Eval` is an inductive relation and the proofs about it proceed by induction on derivations);
at least one clause, unless no rule, `requires` or function applies it (`used`, `appliedSyms`:
then its meaning is never read, and kompile's declared-only symbols, such as macros expanded away,
are admitted; a used function with neither would be read as undefined everywhere, which is not what
the KORE says of it, so it is refused). That two equations of one priority which both apply give
one result is not checked here: `fnExclusiveOK` decides it where it can, and the functions it does not confirm are
`agreeObligations`. A function declared total and not confirmed by `totalOK` is not refused: it is
one of `totalObligations`. -/
def fnOK (heads : List CtorSig) (used : List Sym) (f : Fn) : Bool :=
  f.clauses.all (c.clauseOK f heads) &&
  (!f.clauses.isEmpty || !used.contains f.label)

/-- Every function's clauses, over every function's signature. -/
def fnsOK : Bool := c.fns.all (c.fnOK (c.fns.map Fn.sig) c.appliedSyms)

/-- Each two of f's equations of one priority give one result wherever both apply (`ClausesAgree`,
ClausesAgree.lean; `Det.fnExclusiveOK_sound`), clauses of different priorities never competing
(`Eval.clause`): their patterns are apart
(`overlapList`), or they are alike but for exclusive `requires` (`clausesExclusive`), or their
right-hand sides are one closed term (`clausesAgree`). The second case reads that the first
clause's patterns fix its variables (`clauseFixed`), so that the two clauses' matches at one argument
list are one substitution. `heads` are the functions the `requires` may call, as in `fnOK`. -/
def fnExclusiveOK (heads : List CtorSig) (f : Fn) : Bool :=
  (pairs f.clauses).all (fun (cl, cl') => cl.prio != cl'.prio ||
    !overlapList c.meet c.collHead cl.pats cl'.pats || (c.clauseFixed cl && c.clausesExclusive heads cl cl') ||
      clausesAgree cl cl')

/-- The functions whose equations of one priority `fnExclusiveOK` does not show to agree where two
apply: that they do (`ClausesAgree`) is a named obligation (`Obligations`, Statements.lean). -/
def agreeObligations : List Sym :=
  (c.fns.filter fun f => !c.fnExclusiveOK (c.fns.map Fn.sig) f).map (·.label)

/-- The clauses whose patterns `clauseFixed` does not show to fix their variables, each as its
function and its index among the function's clauses: that each is match independent (two matches
at one argument list give one result, `MatchIndependent`) is a named obligation (`Obligations`,
Statements.lean). -/
def matchObligations : List (Sym × Nat) :=
  c.fns.flatMap fun f =>
    ((List.range f.clauses.length).filter fun i => !(f.clauses[i]?.all c.clauseFixed)).map (f.label, ·)

/-- Every clause of every function, the sort predicates' among them, fixes its variables
(`clauseFixed`): with no agreement named, the clauses of one priority are then coherent
(`Det.coherentAll_of_nil`, FnExclusive.lean), which the executable evaluation's completeness reads
(`EvalTerm.exec`, EvalComplete.lean). -/
def clausesFixed : Bool := c.allFns.all fun f => f.clauses.all c.clauseFixed

/-- The functions declared `[total]` that `totalOK` does not confirm: the functional axiom kompile
writes for each (`∃y. f(x̄) = y`) is not shown to hold of `Eval`, and is a named obligation
(`Obligations`, Statements.lean; KCORE-SPEC.md §2.5). The others are total (`totals_of_order`,
Totals.lean). -/
def totalObligations : List Sym :=
  (c.fns.filter fun f => f.total && !c.totalOK f).map (·.label)

/-- A rule: a left-hand side of the configuration sort whose map patterns have at most one
frame, binding every variable (repetitions allowed); a Bool `requires` and a right-hand side of
the configuration sort over constructors, hooks and the user's functions. -/
def ruleOK (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  sortOfTerm c.patCtx r.vars r.lhs == some topCellSort &&
  noMapIn r.lhs &&
  binds r.vars.length (varOccs r.lhs) &&
  reqOK (c.rhsCtx (c.fns.map Fn.sig)) r.vars r.req &&
  sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx (c.fns.map Fn.sig)) r.vars r.rhs == some topCellSort

/-- A rule, as `ruleOK`, its left-hand side well-sorted over the collection pattern symbols too
(`patCtxAll`). -/
def ruleOKAll (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  sortOfTerm c.patCtxAll r.vars r.lhs == some topCellSort &&
  noMapIn r.lhs &&
  binds r.vars.length (varOccs r.lhs) &&
  reqOK (c.rhsCtx (c.fns.map Fn.sig)) r.vars r.req &&
  sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx (c.fns.map Fn.sig)) r.vars r.rhs == some topCellSort

/-- A clause, as `clauseOK`, its patterns well-sorted over the collection pattern symbols too
(`patCtxAll`: KEVM's `#lookup(K |-> V M, K)`, a list's `ListItem(P) L`). -/
def clauseOKAll (f : Fn) (rhsHeads : List CtorSig) (cl : Clause) : Bool :=
  sortsOfTerms c.patCtxAll cl.vars cl.pats == some f.args &&
  noMapInList cl.pats &&
  binds cl.vars.length (varOccsList cl.pats) &&
  reqOK (c.rhsCtx rhsHeads) cl.vars cl.req &&
  sortOfTerm (c.rhsCtx rhsHeads) cl.vars cl.rhs == some f.result

/-- `fnOK`, its clauses as `clauseOKAll`. -/
def fnOKAll (heads : List CtorSig) (used : List Sym) (f : Fn) : Bool :=
  f.clauses.all (c.clauseOKAll f heads) &&
  (!f.clauses.isEmpty || !used.contains f.label)

def fnsOKAll : Bool := c.fns.all (c.fnOKAll (c.fns.map Fn.sig) c.appliedSyms)

theorem clauseOKAll_of {f : Fn} {H : List CtorSig} {cl : Clause} (h : c.clauseOK f H cl = true) :
    c.clauseOKAll f H cl = true := by
  simp only [clauseOK, clauseOKAll, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨⟨⟨sortsOfTerms_heads _ _ _ _ h.1.1.1.1, h.1.1.1.2⟩, h.1.1.2⟩, h.1.2⟩, h.2⟩

theorem fnsOKAll_of (h : c.fnsOK = true) : c.fnsOKAll = true := by
  simp only [fnsOK, fnsOKAll, List.all_eq_true] at h ⊢
  intro f hf
  have := h f hf
  simp only [fnOK, fnOKAll, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true] at this ⊢
  exact ⟨fun cl hcl => c.clauseOKAll_of (this.1 cl hcl), this.2⟩

theorem ruleOKAll_of {r : Rule} (h : c.ruleOK r = true) : c.ruleOKAll r = true := by
  simp only [ruleOK, ruleOKAll, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨⟨⟨sortOfTerm_heads _ _ _ _ h.1.1.1.1, h.1.1.1.2⟩, h.1.1.2⟩, h.1.2⟩, h.2⟩

end Semantics

/-! ## Certificate and presentation (as F0) -/

/-- A decreasing argument the certificate names is one: its self calls decrease there. A function
with self calls and no decreasing argument is not refused; it is one of `obligations`. -/
def Certificates.ok (z : Certificates) (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  (withPres c.fns z.decreasing).all fun (f, dec) => dec.isNone || decreasingOK c f dec

/-- The functions whose self calls the certificate does not show to decrease: their termination
is a named obligation of any statement that reads it (totality, and the meaning of their equations
as the least one, `Eval`). -/
def Certificates.obligations (z : Certificates) (c : Semantics) : List Sym :=
  ((withPres c.fns z.decreasing).filter fun (f, dec) => !decreasingOK c f dec).map (·.1.label)

def namesFor (n : Nat) (names : List String) : Bool := names.length == n && nodup names

/-- Rule attributes that leave the rule's ground steps unchanged: `concrete` (every ground
configuration is concrete), kompile's `cool-like` and `cool` (hints to a backend's strategy; the
rule is an ordinary rewrite), `preserves-definedness` (a promise to a symbolic backend that the
right-hand side is defined wherever the left-hand side matches; `Step` fires a rule only where its
right-hand side has a value, so the promise changes no step). Not among them: `symbolic` (the rule never fires on ground terms),
`anywhere`, `non-executable`, `simplification`. `owise` and `priority` are not attributes here:
they are read into `Rule.prio`. -/
def inertRuleAttrs : List String := ["concrete", "cool-like", "cool", "preserves-definedness"]

/-- Rule attributes with an argument that only present the rule: those kompile copies from a
production onto its heating and cooling rules. -/
def inertArgAttrs : List String := ["symbol'Kywd'", "format", "colors"]

/-- Strictly increasing. -/
def sortedNat : List Nat → Bool
  | a :: b :: l => decide (a < b) && sortedNat (b :: l)
  | _ => true

/-- The configuration's cell tree: its cells named apart (from each other and the generated ones),
alphanumerically, exactly one leaf `k`, of content K, each with the sorts and symbols of its kind
(`cellIdsShaped`); and the sorts, constructors and subsorts it derives (`Presentation.cellSorts`,
`cellCtors`, `cellSubsorts`) are the first of the core's (`userSorts`, `ctors`, `userSubsorts`),
which `emit` writes from the tree and the rest from the core. -/
def Presentation.cellsOK (p : Presentation) (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  let ns := Semantics.cellNamesList p.config
  nodup (ns ++ ["generatedTop", "generatedCounter"]) && ns.all Semantics.cellNameOK &&
  (Semantics.cellLeavesList p.config).filter (·.1 == "k") == [("k", Srt.k)] && !p.config.isEmpty &&
  Semantics.cellIdsShapedList p.config &&
  p.cellSorts.isPrefixOf c.userSorts && p.cellCtors.isPrefixOf c.ctors &&
  p.cellSubsorts.isPrefixOf c.userSubsorts

/-- The presentation: the core's library is the union of the imported modules' (`libOf`), the
imports increasing; rule attributes inert; a rule's or an equation's priority 50 or 200 unless
written `priority{}("n")`; variable names distinct; the cell tree as `cellsOK` says. -/
def Presentation.ok (p : Presentation) (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.lib == libOf p.imports && sortedNat p.imports &&
  p.rules.all (fun rp => rp.attrs.all inertRuleAttrs.contains && rp.argAttrs.all (inertArgAttrs.contains ·.1)) &&
  (withPres c.rules p.rules).all (fun (r, rp) => rp.prioAttr || r.prio == 50 || r.prio == 200) &&
  ((withPres c.fns p.fns).all fun (f, fp) =>
    (withPres f.clauses fp.clauses).all fun (cl, cp) =>
      namesFor cl.vars.length cp.names && namesFor cl.vars.length cp.exclNames &&
      (cp.prioAttr || cl.prio == 50 || cl.prio == 200)) &&
  ((withPres c.rules p.rules).all fun (r, rp) => namesFor r.vars.length rp.names) &&
  p.cellsOK c

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/FaithOK.lean:
/-
  KCore. The decidable conditions on a semantics that the matching-logic theory `Γ`
  (Faithful.lean) reads beyond `okAll` and `srReady`, joined in one check, `Semantics.faithOK`,
  which `wf` reads (Tie.lean).

  Step soundness (FaithfulSound.lean, `HypSound`) reads that the names and sort numbers of the
  functions are well formed (`namesNumbered`), that values are generated (`genWf`), that no
  collection sort holds a domain value (`collSortsOK`), that the definition's collections are
  built by the parameters their names denote (`collsOK`), and that every symbol a left-hand side
  may apply is one the downward reading covers (`patHeadsOK`). The existence of a model
  (ModelCarrier.lean, `HypModel`) reads in addition that symbols and sorts are named apart
  (`namesApartK`), literals told apart by their text (`LitsApart`), the sorts of values and
  symbols numbered (`sortsNumbered`), collection symbols apart from constructors
  (`collsNotCtors`), symbols named like `ite` apart by their sort (`itesApart`), hooks,
  parameters and constructors apart (`kindsApart`), each constructor listed once (`ctorsOnce`),
  and functions apart from the other kinds (`fnsApart`). The two facts of those hypotheses that
  `wf` decides by its other conjuncts are not repeated: the map pattern symbols are not
  constructors (`patHooksApart`, `NamesApart.patHooks_of_wf`), and the definition's own sorts and
  symbols are numbered (`idsOK`, a conjunct of `namesOK`).
-/
import KcoreSpec.Evaluation
import KcoreSpec.Emit
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Distinct

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

/-- The library collection of a kind (whose hooks a collection sort's symbols have). -/
def builtinColl : CollKind → CollSig
  | .map => builtinColls[0] | .set => builtinColls[1] | .list => builtinColls[2]

namespace Faithful

/-- Every sort the semantics numbers: the registry's and the definition's own. -/
def kernelSorts (c : Semantics) : List Srt := List.range (nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length)

/-- Every symbol the semantics gives a signature: its constructors, its functions (the sort
predicates among them), its parameter symbols and the interpreted hooked symbols. -/
def kernelSyms (c : Semantics) : List CtorSig :=
  c.ctorSigs ++ c.allFns.map Fn.sig ++ c.params.map (·.sig) ++ hookSigs

/-- The constructor sorts: K, KItem, the definition's sorts (the cell sorts among them) and the
library's sorts with generators, less the definition's own collection sorts (`c.colls`). -/
def consSorts (c : Semantics) : List Srt :=
  ([Srt.k, Srt.kitem] ++ sortBy c.sortName (c.userSorts ++ c.libCtorSorts)).filter
    fun s => !(c.colls.any (·.sort == s))

/-- The sorts whose distinct values denote distinct elements: Int, Bool, KConfigVar (whose values
are its tokens, `dvOK`), the library's token and byte sorts, and every collection sort. -/
def distinctSorts (c : Semantics) : List Srt :=
  [Srt.int, Srt.bool, Srt.kconfigVar] ++ c.lib.tokenSorts ++ c.lib.byteSorts ++ c.allColls.map (·.sort)

/-- The value sort of the map collection `k`, at which `Γ` reads its entries' values: its `val`,
and the sort 0 for a collection without one (a set's or a list's axioms read no value sort). -/
def valSort (k : CollSig) : Srt := k.val.getD 0

/-- A sort whose distinct values `Γ` makes distinct elements: K and the sorts below KItem, by the
graph of `_==K_`; the sorts of `distinctSorts`, by the distinctness axiom. -/
def apartSort (c : Semantics) (s : Srt) : Bool :=
  s == Srt.k || s == Srt.kitem || c.sortsBelowKItem.contains s || (distinctSorts c).contains s

/-- **Generated values.** Every constructor's result sort and every subsort pair's upper sort is a
constructor sort, no subsort pair is reflexive, a constructor sort has no domain values and is no
collection sort, and the constructor sorts are `apartSort`. Decidable on the data. It says that a
value of a constructor sort is a constructor or an injection applied to values, which is what makes
the constructors' axioms of `Γ` (read at that sort) describe it, and that distinct values of every
sort are distinct elements (KConfigVar's by `distinctSorts`). -/
def genWf (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.ctorSigs.all (fun k => (consSorts c).contains k.result) &&
  c.subsorts.all (fun p => (consSorts c).contains p.2 && p.1 != p.2) &&
  (consSorts c).all (fun s => apartSort c s && s != Srt.int && s != Srt.bool && s != Srt.kconfigVar &&
    !c.lib.tokenSorts.contains s && !c.lib.byteSorts.contains s && (c.collOf s).isNone)

/-- A collection sort holds no domain value: it is not Int, Bool, KConfigVar, or a token or byte
sort of the library. Decidable on the data. -/
def collSortOK (c : Semantics) (s : Srt) : Bool :=
  s != Srt.int && s != Srt.bool && s != Srt.kconfigVar && !c.lib.tokenSorts.contains s &&
    !c.lib.byteSorts.contains s

/-- Every collection sort of the semantics holds no domain value. -/
def collSortsOK (c : Semantics) : Bool := c.allColls.all fun k => collSortOK c k.sort

/-- The argument sorts of a collection's element symbol: key and value (`valSort`) for a map, the
element sort otherwise. -/
def elemArgs (k : CollSig) : List Srt :=
  match k.kind with
  | .map => [k.key, valSort k]
  | _ => [k.key]

/-- The definition's collection `k` is the collection of its sort (`collOf`), and its unit,
element and concatenation are parameter symbols, not named like a hook or like `ite` at a sort,
whose declarations (the first of their names) have the collection's sorts and are implemented by
the library's symbols of its kind; a map collection has a value sort. Decidable on the data;
`collOK` (which `wf` checks) says that such parameters are declared, this says that they are the
ones the names denote. -/
def collSymsOK (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig) : Bool :=
  decide (c.collOf k.sort = some k) &&
  [k.unit, k.elem, k.concat].all (fun f => !isHook f && (iteSort? (c.symName f)).isNone) &&
  decide (c.lookupParam k.unit = some ⟨⟨k.unit, [], k.sort⟩, some (builtinColl k.kind).unit⟩) &&
  decide (c.lookupParam k.elem = some ⟨⟨k.elem, elemArgs k, k.sort⟩, some (builtinColl k.kind).elem⟩) &&
  decide (c.lookupParam k.concat = some ⟨⟨k.concat, [k.sort, k.sort], k.sort⟩, some (builtinColl k.kind).concat⟩) &&
  (k.kind != .map || k.val.isSome)

/-- A parameter implemented by a map or list pattern symbol: a collection pattern symbol when it
is not a hook (`isCollPat`). -/
def collImpl (kp : ParamSig) : Bool :=
  match kp.impl with
  | some g => patternHooks.contains g || listPatternHooks.contains g
  | none => false

/-- The definition's collections are well formed (`collSymsOK`), and every parameter implemented by
a map or list pattern symbol is the unit, element or concatenation of one of them. Decidable on
the data. -/
def collsOK (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.colls.all (collSymsOK c) &&
  c.params.all fun kp => !collImpl kp ||
    c.colls.any fun k => kp.sig.name == k.unit || kp.sig.name == k.elem || kp.sig.name == k.concat

/-- A pattern symbol the downward reading covers, besides the constructors: a map pattern symbol
or a collection pattern symbol (`isCollPat`: the library list's, the set unit, a parameter
implemented by a map or list pattern symbol). -/
def downHead (c : Semantics) (f : Sym) : Bool := patternHooks.contains f || c.isCollPat f

/-- Every symbol a left-hand side's context gives a signature to (`patCtxAll`) is a constructor
or a symbol the downward reading covers (`downHead`). Decidable on the data. -/
def patHeadsOK (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.patCtxAll.heads.all fun k => c.isCtor k.name || downHead c k.name

/-- The names and sort numbers of the functions are well formed: no constructor or function is
named like `ite` at a sort (`iteSort?`), and every sort of a function is a numbered sort.
`NamesNumbered` (Faithful.lean), decided. -/
def namesNumbered (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.ctorSigs.all (fun k => (iteSort? (c.symName k.name)).isNone) &&
  c.allFns.all (fun fn => (iteSort? (c.symName fn.label)).isNone) &&
  c.allFns.all fun fn => (fn.result :: fn.args).all fun s => decide (s < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length)

namespace Model

/-- `NamesApartK`, decided. -/
def namesApartK (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  (kernelSyms c).all (fun k => (kernelSyms c).all fun k' => c.symName k.name != c.symName k'.name || k == k') &&
  (kernelSyms c).all (fun k => c.symName k.name != "inj") &&
  (kernelSorts c).all (fun s => (kernelSorts c).all fun s' => c.sortName s != c.sortName s' || s == s')

/-- No token or byte sort of the library is Int or Bool: a literal's text then determines the
literal at each sort (`Lit.text` on the literals `dvOK` admits). -/
def LitsApart (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  !(c.lib.tokenSorts ++ c.lib.byteSorts).contains Srt.int &&
  !(c.lib.tokenSorts ++ c.lib.byteSorts).contains Srt.bool

/-- Every sort a value may have, and every sort of a symbol the semantics gives a signature, is a
numbered sort (`kernelSorts`): the sorts of `kernelSyms` (a constructor term has its constructor's
result sort), both sorts of each subsort pair (an injection has its upper one), the library's
token and byte sorts (whose literals are values), and the sorts of every collection. The
interpretation reads a sort by its name among the numbered sorts only, so a value of any other
sort would denote no element of its sort. `NamesNumbered` says this of the functions only, and
`idsOK` of the definition's own sorts only. -/
def sortsNumbered (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  (kernelSyms c).all (fun k => (k.result :: k.args).all fun s => decide (s < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length)) &&
  c.subsorts.all (fun p => decide (p.1 < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length) && decide (p.2 < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length)) &&
  (c.lib.tokenSorts ++ c.lib.byteSorts).all (fun s => decide (s < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length)) &&
  c.allColls.all (fun k => decide (k.sort < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length) &&
    decide (k.key < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length) && decide (valSort k < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length))

/-- No unit, element or concatenation symbol of a collection is a constructor: the interpretation
reads a constructor first, so such a symbol would build a constructor term where the collection's
value is meant. `patHooksApart` says this of the library map's symbols only. -/
def collsNotCtors (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.allColls.all fun k => [k.unit, k.elem, k.concat].all fun f => !c.isCtor f

/-- Every symbol with a signature named like `ite` at a sort (`iteSort?`) is named at a numbered
sort, and no two are named at one sort: `Lblite` applied to a sort reads the first such symbol
(`resolve`), and `Γ` says of each of them what the head `Lblite` applied to its sort does
(`symArityItem`, the graphs of `ΓDomains`), so a sort name that names no sort would leave a
parameter's graph without an element. `iteSort?` drops the last character of the name, so
`namesApartK` does not give the second part. -/
def itesApart (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  (kernelSyms c).all fun k =>
    (match iteSort? (c.symName k.name) with
      | some X => (kernelSorts c).any fun s => c.sortName s == X
      | none => true) &&
    (kernelSyms c).all fun k' =>
      (iteSort? (c.symName k.name)).isNone || iteSort? (c.symName k.name) != iteSort? (c.symName k'.name) || k == k'

/-- The interpreted hooks and the parameters are not constructors, and no parameter is an
interpreted hook: the interpretation reads a constructor first, then a hook, then a parameter, so
a symbol of two kinds would be read as the first, against the graph `Γ` states of the other.
`hooksApart` says this of the user's constructors and functions only, and is not part of `Hyp`. -/
def kindsApart (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  hookSigs.all (fun k => !c.isCtor k.name) &&
  c.params.all (fun kp => !c.isCtor kp.sig.name && !isHook kp.sig.name)

/-- No constructor is listed twice: the names of `ctorSigs` are distinct. `Semantics.gens` reads a
sort's constructors from `ctorSigs`, and `ΓCons` states the distinctness of every pair of them, so
a constructor listed twice is said to be apart from itself (ModelDupCtorWitness.lean).
`namesApartK` does not exclude it: the two entries are one signature. -/
def ctorsOnce (c : Semantics) : Bool := nodup (c.ctorSigs.map (·.name))

/-- No function is named like a constructor, an interpreted hook or a parameter: the interpretation
reads a constructor, then a hook, then a parameter, then a function, so a function of another kind's
name would be read as that symbol, against its equations, and `Γ` has no model when the function's
equation gives the symbol another value than its constructor term (ModelFnCtorWitness.lean).
`idsOK` numbers the user's functions apart from the user's constructors and parameters; the
library's constructors and the registry's parameters are numbered by no check. -/
def fnsApart (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  c.allFns.all fun fn => !c.isCtor fn.label && !isHook fn.label && !c.isParam fn.label

/-! ### `namesApartK` by sorted codes

`namesApartK` compares every two symbols' names, quadratic in their number. `namesApartFast`
decides the same by the strictly ascending sorted codes of the names (`KoreAML.Distinct`): of the
distinct signatures, and of the numbered sorts. -/

/-- The names of the distinct signatures of `kernelSyms` and those of the numbered sorts are
distinct (their codes, sorted, ascend), and no symbol is named `inj`. -/
def namesApartFast (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  let ks := (kernelSyms c).eraseDups
  KoreAML.Distinct.codesDistinct (KoreAML.Distinct.passesFor ks.length) (ks.map fun k => c.symName k.name) &&
  (kernelSyms c).all (fun k => c.symName k.name != "inj") &&
  KoreAML.Distinct.codesDistinct (KoreAML.Distinct.passesFor (kernelSorts c).length)
    ((kernelSorts c).map c.sortName)

theorem kore_nodup_spec : ∀ {l : List String}, KoreAML.nodup l = true → l.Nodup
  | [], _ => List.nodup_nil
  | a :: as, h => by
    simp only [KoreAML.nodup, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
    refine List.nodup_cons.mpr ⟨fun hm => ?_, kore_nodup_spec h.2⟩
    rw [List.contains_iff_mem.mpr hm] at h
    cases h.1

theorem inj_of_nodup_map {α β : Type} {f : α → β} : ∀ {l : List α}, (l.map f).Nodup →
    ∀ x ∈ l, ∀ y ∈ l, f x = f y → x = y
  | [], _, _, hx, _, _, _ => absurd hx List.not_mem_nil
  | a :: l, h, x, hx, y, hy, he => by
    rw [List.map_cons, List.nodup_cons] at h
    rcases List.mem_cons.mp hx with rfl | hx' <;> rcases List.mem_cons.mp hy with rfl | hy'
    · rfl
    · exact absurd (he ▸ List.mem_map_of_mem hy') h.1
    · exact absurd (he.symm ▸ List.mem_map_of_mem hx') h.1
    · exact inj_of_nodup_map h.2 x hx' y hy' he

theorem namesApartK_of_fast {c : Semantics} (h : namesApartFast c = true) : namesApartK c = true := by
  simp only [namesApartFast, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩ := h
  have n1 := kore_nodup_spec (KoreAML.Distinct.nodup_of_codes h1)
  have n3 := kore_nodup_spec (KoreAML.Distinct.nodup_of_codes h3)
  simp only [namesApartK, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true, Bool.or_eq_true, bne_iff_ne, ne_eq,
    beq_iff_eq]
  refine ⟨⟨fun k hk k' hk' => ?_, fun k hk => ?_⟩, fun s hs s' hs' => ?_⟩
  · by_cases he : c.symName k.name = c.symName k'.name
    · exact Or.inr (inj_of_nodup_map n1 k (List.mem_eraseDups.mpr hk) k' (List.mem_eraseDups.mpr hk') he)
    · exact Or.inl he
  · simpa using List.all_eq_true.mp h2 k hk
  · by_cases he : c.sortName s = c.sortName s'
    · exact Or.inr (inj_of_nodup_map n3 s hs s' hs' he)
    · exact Or.inl he

end Model

end Faithful

open Faithful Faithful.Model in
/-- **The decidable conditions of the theory**: what step soundness (`HypSound`) and the existence
of a model (`HypModel`) read of a semantics beyond `okAll`, `srReady`, the map pattern symbols'
apartness from the constructors and the numbering of the definition's own sorts and symbols,
which `wf` decides otherwise. -/
def Semantics.faithOK (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  namesNumbered c && genWf c && collSortsOK c && collsOK c && patHeadsOK c &&
  namesApartK c && LitsApart c && sortsNumbered c && collsNotCtors c && itesApart c &&
  kindsApart c && ctorsOnce c && fnsApart c

open Faithful Faithful.Model in
/-- **The decidable conditions of the theory that soundness and completeness read**: those of
`faithOK` but `collsNotCtors`, which `kindsApart` and `collsOK` imply (`collsNotCtors_of`,
FaithfulCollPat.lean). -/
def Semantics.faithCoreOK (c : Semantics) : Bool :=
  namesNumbered c && genWf c && collSortsOK c && collsOK c && patHeadsOK c &&
  namesApartK c && LitsApart c && sortsNumbered c && itesApart c &&
  kindsApart c && ctorsOnce c && fnsApart c

open Faithful Faithful.Model in
theorem Semantics.faithCoreOK_of_faithOK {c : Semantics} (h : c.faithOK = true) : c.faithCoreOK = true := by
  simp only [Semantics.faithOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩, h4⟩, h5⟩, h6⟩, h7⟩, h8⟩, -⟩, h10⟩, h11⟩, h12⟩, h13⟩ := h
  simp only [Semantics.faithCoreOK, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h10, h11, h12, h13, Bool.and_self]

open Faithful Faithful.Model in
/-- `faithOK` from its conjuncts, the names' apartness by sorted codes (`namesApartFast`): each a
decision of its own. -/
theorem Semantics.faithOK_of_parts {c : Semantics} (h1 : namesNumbered c = true) (h2 : genWf c = true)
    (h3 : collSortsOK c = true) (h4 : collsOK c = true) (h5 : patHeadsOK c = true)
    (h6 : namesApartFast c = true) (h7 : LitsApart c = true) (h8 : sortsNumbered c = true)
    (h9 : collsNotCtors c = true) (h10 : itesApart c = true) (h11 : kindsApart c = true)
    (h12 : ctorsOnce c = true) (h13 : fnsApart c = true) : c.faithOK = true := by
  simp only [Semantics.faithOK, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, namesApartK_of_fast h6, h7, h8, h9, h10, h11, h12,
    h13, Bool.and_self]

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/ModelKindsWitness.lean:
/-
  KCore. A semantics that meets every condition of `coreOK` but `kindsApart`, and `FnHyp`, whose
  `Γ` has no model because an interpreted hook is also a constructor: so `SoundC` fails of it
  (`not_sound`), and `kindsApart` cannot be left out of `coreOK`.

  The library lists the interpreted hook `ite` (`kIte`, `Lblite : Bool KItem KItem → KItem`) among
  its constructors, with the hook's own signature, so `NamesApartK` holds (one name, one
  signature); `hooksApart` reads the user's constructors only. `Γ` says of `Lblite(true, v, v)`,
  by the hook's graph (`ΓDomains`), that it is `v`; read as a constructor's application, it is the
  constructor value `Lblite(true, v, v)`. These are two distinct values of KItem, and `Γ` makes
  distinct values of KItem distinct elements (`values_apart`). The decidable facts are kernel
  decisions.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Sound

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxRecDepth 100000

namespace KCore

namespace Faithful

namespace KindsWitness

open ML

def kIds : CellIds := { sort := nRegSorts, opt := some (nRegSorts + 1), label := nRegSyms + 2, no := some (nRegSyms + 3) }

/-- The configuration `<k> K </k>` with the generated counter, as ordinary sorts, constructors
and subsorts: the top cell's, its fragment's, the `k` cell's and the counter's. -/
def cellSorts : List Srt := [Srt.top, Srt.topFrag, nRegSorts, nRegSorts + 1, Srt.counter, Srt.counterOpt]
def cellCtors : List CtorSig :=
  [⟨topLabel, [nRegSorts, Srt.counter], Srt.top⟩, ⟨topFragLabel, [nRegSorts + 1, Srt.counterOpt], Srt.topFrag⟩,
   ⟨nRegSyms + 2, [Srt.k], nRegSorts⟩, ⟨nRegSyms + 3, [], nRegSorts + 1⟩,
   ⟨counterLabel, [Srt.int], Srt.counter⟩, ⟨noCounter, [], Srt.counterOpt⟩]
def cellSubsorts : List (Srt × Srt) := [(nRegSorts, nRegSorts + 1), (Srt.counter, Srt.counterOpt)]

/-- The interpreted hook `ite`, with its signature. -/
def iteSig : CtorSig := ⟨kIte, [Srt.bool, Srt.kitem, Srt.kitem], Srt.kitem⟩

def c : Semantics :=
  { lib := { ctors := [⟨kconfigValue, [Srt.k], Srt.kitem⟩, iteSig] }
    sortNames := ["KCell", "KCellOpt"]
    symNames := ["LblisKCell", "LblisKCellOpt", "Lbl'-LT-'k'-GT-'", "LblnoKCell"]
    userSorts := cellSorts
    ctors := cellCtors
    fns := []
    userSubsorts := cellSubsorts
    pgmSort := Srt.k
    rules := [] }

theorem sortedOK : c.sortedOK = true := by decide +kernel
theorem srReady : c.srReady = true := by decide +kernel

/-- `c` has no function: `FnHyp` holds. -/
theorem fnHyp : FnHyp c :=
  ⟨fun _ h => absurd h List.not_mem_nil, fun _ h => absurd h List.not_mem_nil,
    fun _ h => absurd h List.not_mem_nil, fun _ h => absurd h List.not_mem_nil⟩

/-- Every condition of `coreOK` but `kindsApart` holds, and `FnHyp`. -/
theorem meets_others : c.sortedOK = true ∧ c.hooksApart = true ∧ c.predsApart = true ∧ c.idsOK = true ∧
    namesNumbered c = true ∧ genWf c = true ∧ collSortsOK c = true ∧ collsOK c = true ∧
    patHeadsOK c = true ∧ Model.namesApartK c = true ∧ Model.LitsApart c = true ∧
    Model.sortsNumbered c = true ∧ Model.itesApart c = true ∧ Model.ctorsOnce c = true ∧
    Model.fnsApart c = true ∧ FnHyp c :=
  ⟨sortedOK, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel,
    by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel,
    by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, by decide +kernel, fnHyp⟩

theorem not_kindsApart : Model.kindsApart c = false := by decide +kernel

/-- `true`. -/
def vb : GroundTerm := .dv Srt.bool (.bool true)
/-- The value `#KConfigValue(.K)`. -/
def vk : GroundTerm := .ctor kconfigValue [.ctor dotk []]
/-- The constructor value `Lblite(true, #KConfigValue(.K), #KConfigValue(.K))`. -/
def vi : GroundTerm := .ctor kIte [vb, vk, vk]

theorem vk_sort : c.sortOf vk = some Srt.kitem := by decide +kernel
theorem vi_sort : c.sortOf vi = some Srt.kitem := by decide +kernel
theorem args_sort : c.sortsOf [vb, vk, vk] = some iteSig.args := by decide +kernel
theorem iteSig_hook : iteSig ∈ hookSigs := by decide +kernel
theorem hook_ite : hook iteSig.name [vb, vk, vk] = some (some vk) := by decide +kernel
theorem genWf_ok : genWf c = true := by decide +kernel
theorem kitem_apart : apartSort c Srt.kitem = true := by decide +kernel
theorem ite_plain : iteSort? (c.symName kIte) = none := by decide +kernel

/-- **`Γ c` has no model.** -/
theorem no_model : ∀ (M : Type) (_ : Inhabited M) (I : Interpretation KoreAML.Sym M), ¬ (I ⊧ᴵP Γ c) := by
  intro M _ I hI
  have hD := defOK hI
  have htr := (sortCtx_of_all sortedOK srReady).trans
  -- the hook's graph: `Lblite(true, v, v)` is `v`
  have hax := sat_dom hI (Or.inl ⟨iteSig, [vb, vk, vk], some vk, iteSig_hook, args_sort, hook_ite, rfl⟩)
  have hgr := (KoreAML.interp_equal hD).mp (hax KoreAML.val0 default)
  -- its left side is the constructor value
  have hfd : ∀ m, (KoreAML.den (symApp c iteSig.name (GroundTerm.koreList c [vb, vk, vk]))).interpret I
      KoreAML.val0 m ↔ (den c vi).interpret I KoreAML.val0 m := fun m => by
    show (KoreAML.den (symApp c kIte _)).interpret I _ m ↔ _
    unfold symApp; rw [ite_plain]; rfl
  have he : elemOf c I vi = elemOf c I vk := by
    have h1 := (elemOf_spec hI vi_sort KoreAML.val0).1
    have h2 := (elemOf_spec hI vk_sort KoreAML.val0).1
    exact (h2 _).mp ((hgr (elemOf c I vi)).mp ((hfd _).mpr ((h1 _).mpr rfl)))
  have := values_apart hI genWf_ok htr kitem_apart vi_sort vk_sort he
  simp only [vi, vk, GroundTerm.ctor.injEq] at this
  exact absurd this.1 (by decide +kernel)

/-- **Soundness fails** of `c`, which meets every condition of `coreOK` but `kindsApart`, and
`FnHyp`. -/
theorem not_sound : ¬ SoundC c := fun h => by
  obtain ⟨⟨M, hM, I, hI⟩, -⟩ := h
  exact no_model M hM I (fun φ hφ => hI φ (Or.inl hφ))

end KindsWitness

end Faithful

end KCore
files.KcoreSpec/EvalFunctional.lean:
/-
  KCore. Evaluation has one result where clauses of one priority are coherent.

  `Eval` reads no order among the clauses of one priority, so it is not functional by construction:
  two clauses of one priority, or two matches of one clause, may both apply at an argument list.
  Clauses of different priorities never compete (the larger one's derivation has the smaller one
  failing, and a clause that applies does not fail). `Coherent` says that two clauses of one
  priority give one result where both apply; with every such pair coherent (`CoherentAll`), a
  function has one result at each argument list (`Eval.functional`). No sorting hypothesis is
  needed.

  The shape of `Coherent` is what the proof, an induction on the first derivation, has in hand:
  - the same instance of one right-hand side (first alternative) is what a syntactic check shows;
    the induction hypothesis for the first clause's right-hand side turns it into one result;
  - one result of the two right-hand sides (second alternative) is the semantic statement, for a
    pair no check confirms;
  - every term inside the first clause's `requires` and right-hand side has one result under its
    match (`HDet`): evaluation is strict, so the first derivation holds a derivation for each of
    them, and the induction hypothesis covers them. Nothing is available for the second clause's
    terms.

  `MatchIndependent` (a clause against itself) and `ClausesAgree` (two clauses of one function)
  are its instances, the obligations `Obligations` names (Statements.lean).
-/
import KcoreSpec.EvalSound

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

open KCore.Exec

/-- The clause applies at `vs` under σ: σ is well sorted, the patterns denote `vs`, and the
`requires` evaluates to `true`. -/
def Clause.AppliesAt (c : Semantics) (cl : Clause) (σ : Subst) (vs : List GroundTerm) : Prop :=
  c.WellSorted cl.vars σ ∧ PatVals c σ cl.pats vs ∧
    ∀ t, cl.req = some t → EvalTerm c σ t (some (bool true))

mutual
  /-- A term and the terms inside it. Evaluation is strict, so a derivation for a term holds one
  for each of them. -/
  def subterms : Term → List Term
    | .var i => [.var i]
    | .dv s l => [.dv s l]
    | .inj a b t => .inj a b t :: subterms t
    | .as t i => .as t i :: subterms t
    | .app f ts => .app f ts :: subtermsList ts
    termination_by structural t => t
  def subtermsList : List Term → List Term
    | [] => []
    | t :: ts => subterms t ++ subtermsList ts
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

theorem self_mem_subterms : ∀ (t : Term), t ∈ subterms t
  | .var _ => List.mem_singleton_self _
  | .dv _ _ => List.mem_singleton_self _
  | .inj _ _ _ => List.mem_cons_self ..
  | .as _ _ => List.mem_cons_self ..
  | .app _ _ => List.mem_cons_self ..

mutual
  theorem subterms_trans {X A : Term} : ∀ {t : Term}, A ∈ subterms t → X ∈ subterms A → X ∈ subterms t
    | .var i, hA, hX => by simp only [subterms, List.mem_singleton] at hA; subst hA; exact hX
    | .dv s l, hA, hX => by simp only [subterms, List.mem_singleton] at hA; subst hA; exact hX
    | .inj a b t, hA, hX => by
      simp only [subterms, List.mem_cons] at hA ⊢
      rcases hA with rfl | hA
      · simpa [subterms] using hX
      · exact .inr (subterms_trans hA hX)
    | .as t i, hA, hX => by
      simp only [subterms, List.mem_cons] at hA ⊢
      rcases hA with rfl | hA
      · simpa [subterms] using hX
      · exact .inr (subterms_trans hA hX)
    | .app f ts, hA, hX => by
      simp only [subterms, List.mem_cons] at hA ⊢
      rcases hA with rfl | hA
      · simpa [subterms] using hX
      · exact .inr (subtermsList_trans hA hX)
    termination_by structural t => t
  theorem subtermsList_trans {X A : Term} : ∀ {ts : List Term}, A ∈ subtermsList ts → X ∈ subterms A →
      X ∈ subtermsList ts
    | [], hA, _ => by simp [subtermsList] at hA
    | t :: ts, hA, hX => by
      simp only [subtermsList, List.mem_append] at hA ⊢
      rcases hA with hA | hA
      · exact .inl (subterms_trans hA hX)
      · exact .inr (subtermsList_trans hA hX)
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

mutual
  /-- The variables of a term inside t are t's. -/
  theorem varOccs_subterms {X : Term} : ∀ {t : Term}, X ∈ subterms t → ∀ i ∈ varOccs X, i ∈ varOccs t
    | .var j, h, i, hi => by simp only [subterms, List.mem_singleton] at h; subst h; exact hi
    | .dv s l, h, i, hi => by simp only [subterms, List.mem_singleton] at h; subst h; exact hi
    | .inj a b t, h, i, hi => by
      simp only [subterms, List.mem_cons] at h
      rcases h with rfl | h
      · exact hi
      · simpa [varOccs] using varOccs_subterms h i hi
    | .as t j, h, i, hi => by
      simp only [subterms, List.mem_cons] at h
      rcases h with rfl | h
      · exact hi
      · simp only [varOccs, List.mem_append]; exact .inl (varOccs_subterms h i hi)
    | .app f ts, h, i, hi => by
      simp only [subterms, List.mem_cons] at h
      rcases h with rfl | h
      · exact hi
      · simpa [varOccs] using varOccsList_subterms h i hi
    termination_by structural t => t
  theorem varOccsList_subterms {X : Term} : ∀ {ts : List Term}, X ∈ subtermsList ts →
      ∀ i ∈ varOccs X, i ∈ varOccsList ts
    | [], h, _, _ => by simp [subtermsList] at h
    | t :: ts, h, i, hi => by
      simp only [subtermsList, List.mem_append] at h
      simp only [varOccsList, List.mem_append]
      rcases h with h | h
      · exact .inl (varOccs_subterms h i hi)
      · exact .inr (varOccsList_subterms h i hi)
    termination_by structural ts => ts
end

/-- `u` has one result under σ. -/
def Fun (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) (u : Term) : Prop :=
  ∀ r r', EvalTerm c σ u r → EvalTerm c σ u r' → r = r'

/-- One result is a property of the values of a term's variables. -/
theorem Fun.congr {c : Semantics} {σ σ' : Subst} {u : Term}
    (ha : ∀ i ∈ varOccs u, σ.lookup i = σ'.lookup i) (h : Fun c σ' u) : Fun c σ u :=
  fun r r' h1 h2 => h r r' (EvalTerm.congr h1 ha) (EvalTerm.congr h2 ha)

/-- Every term inside `t` has one result under σ. -/
def HDet (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) (t : Term) : Prop := ∀ u ∈ subterms t, Fun c σ u

/-- Two clauses (or one clause twice) are coherent: where both apply at one argument list, they
are the same instance of one right-hand side, or their right-hand sides have the same result. The
one who shows it may use that the terms of the first clause's `requires` and right-hand side each
have one result under its match. -/
def Coherent (c : Semantics) (cl cl' : Clause) : Prop :=
  ∀ vs σ σ', cl.AppliesAt c σ vs → cl'.AppliesAt c σ' vs →
    (∀ t, cl.req = some t → HDet c σ t) → HDet c σ cl.rhs →
    (cl.rhs = cl'.rhs ∧ ∀ i ∈ varOccs cl.rhs, σ.lookup i = σ'.lookup i) ∨
    ∀ r r', EvalTerm c σ cl.rhs r → EvalTerm c σ' cl'.rhs r' → r = r'

/-- Every two clauses of one priority of every function are coherent, each clause with itself
among them. -/
def CoherentAll (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  ∀ f fn, c.lookupFn f = some fn → ∀ cl ∈ fn.clauses, ∀ cl' ∈ fn.clauses, cl.prio = cl'.prio →
    Coherent c cl cl'

/-- Two matches of the clause at one argument list give one result: the clause is coherent with
itself. -/
def MatchIndependent (c : Semantics) (cl : Clause) : Prop := Coherent c cl cl

/-- Every clause of every function is match independent. -/
def MatchIndependentAll (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  ∀ f fn, c.lookupFn f = some fn → ∀ cl ∈ fn.clauses, MatchIndependent c cl

namespace EvalFunctional

variable {c : Semantics}

abbrev M1 (c : Semantics) (f : Sym) (vs : List GroundTerm) (r : Option GroundTerm) : Prop :=
  ∀ r', Eval c f vs r' → r = r'
abbrev M2 (c : Semantics) (vs : List GroundTerm) (cl : Clause) : Prop :=
  ∀ σ, cl.AppliesAt c σ vs → False
abbrev M3 (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) (cl : Clause) : Prop :=
  (∀ t, cl.req = some t → EvalTerm c σ t (some (bool true))) → False
abbrev M4 (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) (t : Term) (r : Option GroundTerm) : Prop :=
  (∀ r', EvalTerm c σ t r' → r = r') ∧ HDet c σ t
abbrev M5 (c : Semantics) (σ : Subst) (ts : List Term) (rs : List (Option GroundTerm)) : Prop :=
  (∀ rs', EvalTerms c σ ts rs' → rs = rs') ∧ ∀ u ∈ subtermsList ts, Fun c σ u

theorem mk4 {σ : Subst} {t : Term} {r : Option GroundTerm}
    (top : ∀ r', EvalTerm c σ t r' → r = r')
    (sub : ∀ u ∈ subterms t, u = t ∨ Fun c σ u) : M4 c σ t r :=
  ⟨top, fun u hu => (sub u hu).elim (fun h => h ▸ fun _ _ h1 h2 => (top _ h1).symm.trans (top _ h2)) id⟩

/-- A clause that applies under σ, its `requires` having one result there, does not fail. -/
theorem not_fails {vs : List GroundTerm} {cl : Clause} {σ : Subst}
    (hσ : c.WellSorted cl.vars σ) (hmatch : PatVals c σ cl.pats vs)
    (ihreq : ∀ t, cl.req = some t → M4 c σ t (some (bool true))) (hf : Fails c vs cl) :
    False := by
  cases hf with
  | intro h =>
    cases h σ hσ hmatch with
    | intro ht he hr => exact hr ((ihreq _ ht).1 _ he).symm

theorem case_clause (hco : CoherentAll c) {f : Sym} {fn : Fn} {vs : List GroundTerm}
    {cl : Clause} {σ : Subst} {r : Option GroundTerm}
    (hfn : c.lookupFn f = some fn) (hmem : cl ∈ fn.clauses)
    (hσ : c.WellSorted cl.vars σ) (hmatch : PatVals c σ cl.pats vs)
    (hreq : ∀ t, cl.req = some t → EvalTerm c σ t (some (bool true)))
    (hrhs : EvalTerm c σ cl.rhs r)
